the rapporteur. - madam president, madam commissioner, i do not think i will be using the four minutes, because at this time of night and with so many members, there is no need to give many explanations. but it is a report on a subject which in the next ten or fifteen years will revolutionize the relationship between people and objects and between objects and objects: a new application of the internet. i should like to welcome the communication which the commission has drawn up, because it is an opportunity to anticipate the consequences of this new application, which have many virtues: they can improve many aspects of our lives, they open up new business opportunities and improve production. but they also, of course, have their risks. as for the report on which i have worked, together with the alternative rapporteurs from other political groups - to whom i would like to thank for their work - we have tried to ensure that users have all the security and privacy they are concerned about when using these new technologies. we have been looking at whether the legal framework covers all the possibilities that these new applications open up and, at the moment, it seems that it does, but what has been decided is that it should be evaluated. as these applications are being incorporated into different facets of our lives, they have to be evaluated, to see that, really, the users have their privacy and their security covered, from the point of view of health, but also from the point of view of privacy and so many, many issues. i think that's a good approach. this is just the beginning. and perhaps, apart from what the report says, madam commissioner, we should think about how we inform users well so that they really know what it is about. because, the truth is that not only users but also most of the members of this house who are not concerned with these issues, when we talk about the internet of things, they look at us with a face as if saying, and what is this? i think it would be interesting, apart from all these possibilities and concerns that the report - and also its communication - contains, to think carefully about how we are going to explain to people, to citizens, to users, what the internet of things is and what they can do with these new applications and how their privacy and security are covered. i think that is the point of this new application: that citizens trust it, that they feel safe.
the rapporteur, mrs schleicher, has already said that the internet is a global public good which must be managed in the general interest. the network is based on a public-private model and must be prevented from being controlled by any entity or group of entities, and any attempt by state or supranational authorities to control the flow of information accessing the network. a key concern of this report has been the position of the internet corporation for assigned names and numbers (icann) in the global governance of the internet. as a private institution governed by us law, we have emphasized its uniqueness in view of the delicate role it plays and, while we support its maintenance because its work has been generally effective, we advocate a reform that would allow for greater participation by the european institutions in its governing bodies. but the internet is above all an essential instrument for the exercise of fundamental freedoms and for the enjoyment of genuinely democratic citizenship. significant safeguards against new forms of surveillance, control and censorship by public or private actors should therefore be established so that freedom of access to the internet and the protection of privacy are real and not illusory. in particular, governments are asked to refrain from restricting internet access through censorship, blocking, filtering or other means, and from entrusting private entities to carry out these activities. restrictions deemed indispensable, for example for the protection of minors, must be limited to what is strictly necessary in a democratic society, must be based on law and must respect the principle of proportionality as developed by the court of justice of the european union and the court of human rights. internet access must be made available to all citizens in an effective manner and, above all, without discrimination, with a special effort being made in relation to people living in rural areas, in the terms, incidentally, already provided for in the digital agenda approved by this parliament. we believe that it is very important that europe's voice is heard united and strong in internet governance, both in icann and in other international forums, especially in the internet governance forum, as it is a powerful instrument for dialogue between governments, civil society and the private sector. the next session of this forum is to be held in september in vilnius and its importance has not gone unnoticed by those of us who have written this report, so we strongly support it, while proposing some corrections to its working methods. in these scenarios it is very important that the principles of the european union as expressed in article 2 of its treaty are upheld, especially our relations with countries whose values may differ from those of europeans. the internet is the great sea, the ocean that must unite free citizens. i would like to thank the members who have worked with me on this report and the officials on the committee who have been of invaluable assistance. thank you very much for your attention at this time of night.

in writing. − we greens have strongly supported this report by our socialist colleague, badia i cutchet. it will be an important new application of internet technology. in the next 10-15 years, it is predicted that the internet of things will enter our daily lives. it uses rfid (radio frequency identification) technology to receive and transmit information wirelessly. it works with a tiny chip which has the capacity to store a lot of information about the object or the person on which it has been placed. in the agri-food sector, for example, rfid allows better and faster product traceability, and provides information about content: chemical characteristics, gluten levels, etc. similar applications are already in use, such as a chip that can convey real-time information about tyre pressure to a driver. this new technology will revolutionise and widen person-to-thing and thing-to-thing interaction. the innovation lies in the thing-to-thing relationship. the most commonly cited practical example of this is that of fridges which, if suitably programmed, will be able to detect any product past, or approaching, its use-by date.

president of the commission. − speaking frankly, i am not looking at this point in terms of a fight for competence or grabbing power. that is not the problem. what we have now, and it is clear – article 120 of the treaty – is a situation in which the economic policy of a member state is not just a matter of national concern. we have seen during this crisis that the decisions taken by one country have a very direct spill-over effect on the other countries. so it makes sense, for instance, that the member states, when they are preparing their budget, know what others are doing as well, because the decisions of others will have an impact on their own decisions. we do not want at all – and i want to make this clear – to interfere in the sovereign powers of our national parliaments. it is very important for this to be respected, but it makes sense that when we are discussing the economic policy for europe – and we have seen how interdependent we are – we should be aware of what the main intentions of the other economies are. this is the right point. what is the added value of being together? this is the sensible line the commission is proposing, and we believe that now a consensus is emerging along these lines.
president of the commission. − you are completely right when you underline what i have been calling the holistic approach to economic policy. it is a mistake and i think now member states are well aware of it. when we speak about economic policy in europe, just to consider the stability and growth pact or just to consider the financial services reform, it all comes down to growth. to have sustainable growth, we need of course to have sound economic governance in europe, we have to respect the stability and growth pact, and we need the credibility of sound public finances, but we also need new regulatory supervision for the financial market and we need to invest in our potential for growth. this is precisely what eu 2020 is about. it is about reform. that is why i am insisting that we need fiscal consolidation and structural reform. and of course we need to pursue the economic policies that are so important for us in europe, namely in terms of economic and social cohesion – not only for 16 – or 17, because i hope that estonia will join the euro area very soon – but for all the 27 member states.
president of the commission. − you have raised many questions. first of all, what we are doing now in the task force and indeed in the commission – a communication on 12 may already mentioned this – is examining the possibility of reinforcing the stability and growth pact, including by broadening the arsenal of incentives for compliance, as i prefer to call it. i believe it makes sense to have these incentives for compliance – some people speak of sanctions – because we need the credibility of those instruments to ensure that the stability and growth pact is respected. as we have seen, the problem was that some member states did not respect the treaty that they themselves had adopted and ratified. how can we do this? we want to do it in a fair manner, not just penalising those countries that are in the cohesion fund. that is why we are looking for ways of implementing those incentives for compliance, irrespective of whether or not the countries are cohesion countries. those incentives for compliance can be reinforced in several ways, for instance more upstream, including using them in the preventive part of the pact, or more consequently, for instance with an increased degree of automaticity. we are looking at several ways and the commission will put forward some legislative proposals on this.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should first like to thank very sincerely the political groups who have taken the initiative of this series of questions on an extremely important subject, mr chountis, mr pittella, mr gauzès, and now mrs goulard, and other members who will be speaking. i would like to give you my honest opinion and i hope you will appreciate my determination on this and other issues relating to the lessons of the crisis and the transparency to which citizens and businesses are entitled. i had the opportunity on 20 april to raise the issue of credit rating agencies and their importance for the functioning of the economy and the financial markets. when it comes to checking the health or fever of a product, a company, or a state - i will come back to that - when it comes to sovereign risks, madam goulard, ladies and gentlemen, you will agree with me that breaking the thermometer does not eliminate fever. the question is whether the thermometer is working properly and, if so, whether we can use several thermometers to do the validation and the checks. and my feeling is that there is a lot to be said about how the thermometer works, and therefore how the rating agencies work, which play a leading role in assessing the risks of the situation of companies as well as states. the crisis has shown, and it shows, mr chountis, you are right, that their functioning has not always been exemplary, with sometimes very serious consequences. this is an area, ladies and gentlemen, in which the g20 has taken strong decisions, as on other subjects, in this case to put in place supervision and governance rules. and i want to remind you that at the time of the crisis, as many of you have pointed out, mr gauzès, mrs goulard, the commission quickly took up its responsibilities and made the regulation of the activities of the rating agencies a priority over the last two years. as early as september 2009, one year after lehman's bankruptcy, the regulation on credit rating agencies was adopted, with very strong support, support and improvements from parliament - i thank mr gauzès again - to address the problems raised by the way these agencies operated, which contributed in some way to the financial crisis. the regulation introduced a mandatory registration regime for all agencies established in the union and imposed a set of stringent requirements to ensure that potential conflicts of interest are eliminated as far as possible, to enhance the quality of ratings and the methodology for rating and, finally, to ensure that agencies act in a more transparent manner. ladies and gentlemen, i am confident that these new rules will significantly improve the independence and integrity of the rating process, the transparency of these rating activities and the quality of the ratings themselves, including the ratings of the sovereign debt of the countries of the european union and of the financial institutions of the union. two weeks ago, in the second stage, on 2 june, the commission, on my proposal, adopted a proposal to amend the regulation on credit rating agencies to give esma, the future european financial market authority, exclusive competence for the registration and ongoing supervision of credit rating agencies. it is still necessary for esma to exist, and i fully agree with what has just been said by mrs goulard and what you all think, that we must - we were talking about this recently with the rapporteurs on the supervision package, the larosière package - reach a dynamic, credible compromise between parliament and the council to implement what has been proposed, namely the establishment of these three independent authorities by 1 january next. we're not there yet. we must make an effort, and i call again from this platform and from the council and parliament to bring their views closer together. and i repeat, mr president, the commission's readiness, and my readiness in particular, to promote this dynamic compromise. in addition, in order to enhance the benefit of transparency and increase competition among credit rating agencies, a provision has been introduced to facilitate access to information on structured finance instruments by any credit rating agency interested in publishing an unsolicited rating. in other words, when one structured products agency receives information to develop its rating, the other agencies will have the right to use this information to develop their own ratings. so here we are. that's not enough. it is increasingly widely recognised in europe and around the world that the current failures affecting the rating procedures, which have been brought to light by the crisis, have not been adequately addressed, and i want to agree with mr chountis on this analysis. that is why i have asked my services to undertake a new reflection on the whole architecture and role of rating agencies. it is in this context, mr pittella, that the analysis, the very precise, objective examination of the functioning of these agencies in the light of the new regulations will be carried out in the coming months - you said an inquiry - and taking account of this, even if it is not fully implemented, it will have to wait until the beginning of december. i think, as you all do, ladies and gentlemen, that there is a problem simply with the diversity of this market. this market is too concentrated, in too few hands. there is not enough competition in this sector, and that is a matter of concern to us. without, for the moment, favouring any particular option, mr pittella, the commission is considering structural measures, including the creation of an independent european rating agency which, for some of us, i say now on a personal basis, is rather my favourite, particularly as regards the rating of sovereign risks mentioned by mr gauzès earlier, such as mrs goulard or mr pittella. another structural measure we are considering is the increased involvement of independent public entities in the rating process. the sovereign debt, since this is what is at stake when we talk about greece and, if necessary, other states, must be given special attention to ensure that the methods used are the right ones and that they are appropriate. the lack of due diligence by banks and other financial institutions, the lack of alternative criteria for assessing the reliability of an investment also deserve particular attention. the current financial regulations which expressly provide for the use of ratings also require a thorough review. these are all subjects, and we will not avoid any of the difficult issues on which the commission is working. we will be able to give our first guidelines in september, at the same time as we deal with other important issues of transparency and control, in terms of the regulation of derivatives and short selling. and we will make legislative proposals at the end of this year or at the very beginning of 2011, not only, madame goulard, to continue - i quote your own words - what was started by my predecessor with your support, which is being put in place and which is not enough, but also to amplify, go further towards transparency to avoid conflicts of interest, and for these ratings to be more numerous, more diversified and, as far as sovereign risks are concerned, unchallenged.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner barnier, the rating agencies were not able to anticipate the subprime mortgage crisis, the risk of structured finance products or the collapse of lehman brothers. the regulation adopted in april 2009 promotes their transparency, subjects the agencies themselves to european oversight and begins to address issues relating to their responsibility and quality, addressing some conflicts of interest in their operations. the commission's new proposal is a further step in this direction. i am convinced that we in parliament will contribute to the establishment of supervision from 1 january 2011 and, moreover, to cooperation in its projects, so that there is a new, stricter regulatory framework. the role that regulatory agencies are now playing in the debt and public deficit crisis, revealing the discretion of their ratings in terms of methods, preparation and communication, the high procyclical impact of their ratings - sometimes said to be firefighters, what they do is to fan the flames further - their collision with the positions of the main international and european financial institutions - to the point that the european central bank has decided to dispense with their ratings in sovereign debt operations - require a more thorough rethinking of their role and comparison with the general interests. today, there is open doubt as to whether rating agencies are capable of making an objective and responsible assessment, in particular of sovereign risk, and the questions that arise are of a deeper nature - as you said, of a structural nature - and affect their compatibility with democratic principles, because they affect the efforts that pensioners, workers and the vulnerable population are making and who do not want to see them fail and be trampled underfoot by irresponsibility in the functioning of the markets. these are questions that affect independence. is public rating compatible with private ownership? can you be both judge and jury? is it possible to qualify as a business model based on remuneration paid by the actors themselves to be examined? are the actors the ones who get to choose the examiner? the united states senate is already addressing these issues and it would be necessary for us to address them here as well. these are issues that affect responsibility and sustainability. can responsible governance be ensured that avoids short-term perspectives and ensures sustainability? can the agencies remain indifferent to the commitments of the european authorities and to the efforts of the main international public actors? will they be held responsible for their effects on the market, especially their consequences, which, i agree with you, can be described as harmful? will they maintain regulatory privileges and a regulatory reliance on the standards that appeal to the use of their qualifications? will the lack of competition continue? and, in the legitimacy aspect, can agencies hold so much sway over our economies with so little control? is it necessary to go beyond supervisory control and go to the internal control of the governance structure and even the business structure itself? a public european rating system should be established, a new role for existing european agencies should be forced, new ones should be promoted and even the need for a global rating should be raised, in accordance with new principles. these are the questions that must be answered, commissioner.

member of the commission. − the eu habitats and birds directives as they stand provide the necessary flexibility to ensure compatibility between nature protection and economic development. the commission does not believe that a review would be justified at this stage. the reasons are as follows: the eu nature legislation sets a global model for nature protection – science-driven, legally enforceable and based upon ecosystems as the basic unit. the natura network is one of the most advanced, most extensive and most flexible systems of nature protection in the world. it is one of the greatest achievements of european union environmental policy. biodiversity is a key environmental priority for the commission during its present term. in march this year the council reaffirmed that protected areas and ecological networks are a cornerstone of our efforts to preserve biodiversity and stressed the need to fully implement the birds and habitats directives and speed up completion of the natura 2000 network. we are now at a crucial stage of implementation of the legislation. across europe the process of designation of natura 2000 sites is nearing completion and the priority is now to ensure that the natura 2000 network is effectively managed and properly resourced so that it can fully achieve its objectives. the eu habitats directive is a unique, flexible tool, which allows farming, fishing, forestry, hunting and even major development projects to be carried out in a way that does not destroy the ecological value of our natural heritage. natura sites are not no-go areas where human activities and economic development are to be excluded. most sites are living landscapes which have been shaped as a result of many years of human intervention. designation of a natura site does not mean that economic activities within the site must be frozen. on the contrary, there are many examples such as the port of antwerp – which i visited recently and which is also mentioned in your question – where economic development successfully continues side by side with nature protection. correct implementation of the provisions of the nature directives, early integration of environmental concerns into the planning process and broad information and involvement of all stakeholders are key to such success stories. finally, in view of the fact that we have not met the political target of halting the loss of biodiversity in 2010, we will have to assess the reasons why we have failed. in that context, we will also need to evaluate in detail whether implementation of our existing legislation is effective in delivering biodiversity protection and reflect on what improvements should eventually be made.

the next item is the report by mr raül romeva i rueda, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a catch documentation programme for bluefin tuna (thunnus thynnus) and amending regulation (ec) no 1984/2003 (com (2009) 0406 - c7-0124/2009 - 2009/0116 (cod)) (a7-0119/2010).
the rapporteur. - mr president, i think that at this stage it is no longer a secret to anyone that the value of this animal is very high, especially in some markets, such as the asian markets. in fact, it is so precious that some traders have cheated and continue to cheat. each year iccat adopts increasingly complex and restrictive management measures, recovery plans, documentation systems, vessel capacity restrictions, and each year the european commission congratulates iccat on its success, stating that the organisation has finally taken the necessary measures to reduce the bluefin tuna 'you-you' fishery and that the situation is under control. but time passes and the measures supposedly designed to ensure their conservation, or better still, their recovery, either do not arrive, or they arrive too late and inadequately. the premature closure of the fishing season for the purse seine fleet just a few days ago, because the quota allocated to the european union had been 'almost' used up in just 10 days, shows that there is still a problem of overcapacity in europe and that this is a major threat to the survival of the species. the stocks have not shown the necessary signs of recovery in the medium term, on the contrary. the situation of over-exploitation of the two bluefin tuna stocks is well known. the spawning biomass of both stocks has been reduced to less than 15% of the uncaught biomass. this, combined with the high prices paid for fish, whether legally caught or not, and the evident difficulties in controlling fishing and trade activities, shows that these efforts of iccat over the last 20 years are, at the very least, insufficient. the commission has already taken a number of decisions on the basis of the proposals contained in the report. the report we are voting on today is one more, indispensable, undoubtedly necessary and yet insufficient measure. this new regulation, which i am glad to have agreed with the various institutions, is intended to combat illegal fishing for bluefin tuna and to improve the control of bluefin tuna stocks. this system requires that each batch of tuna must be accompanied by the required documentation at each stage, from the moment of its capture, including landing, transhipment, caging, slaughter, import, export and re-export. the documentation must be validated at each stage by the authorities of the competent state, flag state, trap or cage and must include information such as catch data, information on the exporter or seller, information on transhipment, details of the fattening facility, information on slaughter, commercial information in short. after the frustration of many people, including myself, that cites did not include bluefin tuna in its list of endangered species at its last meeting, the ball is now back on the icca roof. we have a new opportunity in november, in paris, to see how decisive the situation is and, above all, to assume that there is no longer time for further extensions, for legal tricks or for false optimistic speeches. in paris we will see whether this time the contracting parties - and the european union is one of them - are really committed, in a strict and scrupulous way, to the scientific recommendations. i know of your personal commitment, commissioner damanaki, and you will have our full support to support precisely this line. this is probably the only chance we have of making real and serious progress in solving this problem, because if we do not, we have another opportunity later, a more drastic, a more difficult one, which will be to bring the matter back to the cites table. the next meeting will be in 2013 and let us not forget that if we do not find the necessary solutions and commitment at cicaa in november, cites will remain and must be a new door to which we must knock when it is appropriate.
acting president of the council. - mr president, i would first like to point out the importance which the spanish presidency attaches to the presentation of this proposal for a regulation for formal agreement at this plenary session of the european parliament. this is important for two reasons, as i shall explain below. the council regulation establishing a catch documentation programme for bluefin tuna and amending regulation (ec) no 1984/2003 incorporates into community legislation, with all the guarantees, iccat recommendations 07-10 and 08-12 establishing the catch documentation programme for bluefin tuna, and in particular iccat recommendation 09-11, which was adopted at the last meeting in recife in november last year and which has also been applicable since 1 june. all these recommendations are in line with the view that the catch document is the key and primary element for the correct identification and full monitoring of bluefin tuna catches. this makes it possible to ensure traceability and to be sure that the tuna consumed comes from controlled catches, made under conditions that ensure its sustainability and under the measures set out in the recovery plan adopted for this species. this control scheme in practice means that every batch of bluefin tuna must be accompanied at every stage of the chain, up to its consumption, by a catch document duly validated by the authorities of the flag state of the fishing vessel, irrespective of the mode of origin, whether from the farm or from the workstation. this new proposal also aims to take account of all the activities related to the catching and fattening of bluefin tuna, and thus to cover all possible cases and situations in order to avoid loopholes where less responsible actions could escape control and jeopardise the whole effort we are making to recover bluefin tuna. in this way, the catch document will allow monitoring of all marketing operations of bluefin tuna from the time of its capture until it reaches the plate and thus the guarantee that the tuna has been caught under the control and surveillance of the competent authorities of the flag state. this document is therefore a very important instrument in the control of bluefin tuna fisheries and the fight against illegal, unregulated and unregulated fishing. i would also point out that this improvement in traceability in the bluefin tuna fishery will also have a clear effect on the scientific evaluation of this stock, since we will have better information on this fishery, which will result in more reliable and reliable scientific evaluations of its situation. apart from the importance of this regulation for the improvement of the instruments for monitoring the bluefin tuna fishery, the spanish presidency is also pleased that it was possible to reach agreement on this regulation at first reading. this shows the interest and willingness of both institutions - the council and the european parliament - to bring forward legislative proposals on fisheries in the shortest possible time. the adoption of this report by this house, which is scheduled for today, will enable it to be finally adopted, as point a, by the council of fisheries ministers on 29 june in luxembourg. i would like to thank all of you for your valuable contributions to the drafting of this text and i hope that it will serve as an example for future proposals, which will have to be adopted under the codecision procedure under the lisbon treaty.
member of the commission. − mr president, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr romeva i rueda, for his work on this report. i am pleased to see the strong support of the fisheries committee on this important proposal. the implementation of the iccat bluefin tuna catch documentation programme is indeed a key measure to prevent, deter and eliminate iuu fishing. i am delighted that the report in particular supports all aspects linked to the practical implementation of the catch documentation which must accompany bluefin tuna products from catch to the trade channel. inspired by the current practices in other regional fisheries management organisations and custom regulations, this catch documentation scheme can only be efficient if applied to all bluefin tuna products, including processed and farmed products. this will ensure the control of traceability of bluefin tuna fishery products landed, farmed, domestically traded, imported or exported from the european union. i would like also to inform you that the commission agrees with nearly all the amendments proposed, most of them resulting from the trilogue between the european parliament, the council and the commission. i would once again like to thank mr romeva i rueda for the report and the fisheries committee for the time spent on this important issue. this report is a significant contribution to a truly efficient traceability system for bluefin tuna and an effective fight against iuu activities.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work and on the ease with which he has allowed us all to work with him and to produce a good report. and we are also pleased that, for the first time, we are going to adopt a report on fisheries, under the ordinary legislative procedure, at first reading and with the agreement of the three institutions. the amendments by parliament are mainly aimed at incorporating the new recommendations made at the 2009 meeting of the iccat, as the commission's original proposal only included the 2008 recommendations, and at clarifying and specifying some technical definitions and specifications in order to make the obligations of all operators and each member state involved in bluefin tuna fisheries crystal clear. the aim is to identify the origin of all bluefin tuna entering the eu markets so that, if this origin cannot be ascertained, the marketing of the tuna is prohibited. we have thus obtained, as the rapporteur himself acknowledges in his report, the most complete catch documentation programme for any species, which allows us to send a message of confidence, recalling that the international organisation which regulates the management of bluefin tuna is very capable of reacting on its own in monitoring its situation and in dealing with the illegal fishing networks of a species whose trade has reached a complexity not found in any other species. it is doubtful that, despite the criticism, without the knowledge and experience acquired by iccaa, any other body could have taken such measures with the same knowledge and speed. we therefore hope that the entry into force of this regulation will help not only to restore the species and to combat illegal exploitation, but also to restore a minimum of rationality and objectivity to public opinion and, in particular, to some non-governmental organizations. as the rapporteur has said, the ball goes back to the iccaa, and i would add: it goes back to the iccaa, fortunately, where it should never have left. and i say this on behalf of my group.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, we are in the midst of a historic debate. for the first time, parliament exercises the co-decision powers granted to it by the lisbon treaty in the fisheries sector. and it has special significance for those of us who, like myself, live in a fishing community or who appreciate that it has been carried out under the spanish presidency. full participation of direct representatives of citizens in the legislative process strengthens democratic life in the union and increases the legitimacy, quality and effectiveness of the european fisheries policy. this legislative procedure concerns bluefin tuna, a species whose biological status is a matter of concern because it is at risk of extinction and therefore deserves priority attention. the iccat is the regional organisation responsible for fisheries management. its measures, based on scientific reports on the state of the resources, should contribute to their recovery and sustainability. the provisions we adopt today incorporate their recommendations on catch documentation. this is an essential element for the protection and management of resources, for their effectiveness. ensuring traceability from catch to the final stage of the marketing process is essential to combat illegal fishing and trade and, consequently, to promote sustainable fishing and responsible trade. its implementation will make better and stricter control possible by the european union. the international commitments have been incorporated in full fidelity, without any changes that would distort them. in addition, to allow for a dynamic reception of future adaptations, the new possibilities of the lisbon treaty to delegate to the commission powers to implement new conservation measures have been used. for all that, i am satisfied with the result. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr romeva, and the other members with whom i have co-signed the text to be put to the vote today.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, the other groups, the council and the commission for the agreement we have reached at first reading. this regulation, which has been improved by the amendments tabled by the various parliamentary groups, transposes into community law all the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccaa). it involves the establishment of a stricter certification system in order to improve the control of bluefin tuna catches, to eliminate illegal fishing and to improve the quality and availability of statistical data, which are so necessary for its control. it is intended to control the tracking of the product from its capture to its placing on the market - in short, to control its traceability - a measure which is necessary for greater protection of bluefin tuna, taking account of recovery plans for bluefin tuna, and for better protection, given the situation in which we find ourselves at the moment. finally, i would like to stress that this is the first time that parliament has used its decisionmaking power since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and i hope that it will not be the last, given the bad experience we have had in other cases.
i would like to thank mr romeva for his report, which really emphasizes the need to protect tuna. i think there is only about 15% left of the entire bluefin tuna population. i think that the bluefin tuna, which we have been working on for many years in this house to prevent its disappearance, is quite a symbol, is it not? it is a symbol that has a lot to do with what is happening in the european union, with what is happening to all europeans. what happens when the market is not regulated? when the market is not regulated, jobs and species and the environment are put first. this is a principle which, unfortunately, we have to suffer from. the workers and the species have to suffer, and the planet as a whole, climate change. when the market is not regulated, it is obviously insatiable, until resources are exhausted. that is why this report, with the help of the commission and the council, is so important. what's the point? so that we can put a stop to industrial techniques, to predatory techniques which do not take into account the need to maintain the natural environment and species. and they can't pay the righteous for the sinners. mr romeva knows my position on the need not to punish the mattresses. i know that the cod is an ancient fishing technique that has never put tuna at risk - and mr romeva shares this view - and it is therefore a matter of the european union taking seriously all the technical reports and recommendations on catch documentation and traceability in paris in november, so that we can all make work compatible with the natural environment, which is a fundamental principle that should be part of the values of the european union.
mr president, congratulations, mr romeva, on bringing us all together. and i really want to talk about your report, because we always talk about tuna, about sustainability criteria, we link it to illegal fishing, to a fraudulent situation and, however, we do not see the positive side, which is the determination of the population and its compliance, which is what each state must do and we must be vigilant. but this report, which is fighting against illegality, is also a complement to the instruments of security, because it is the quality of work that will be examined here, the control measures. this is the implementation of an international decision, it is the most rigorous way of guaranteeing commitment, and i am pleased, mr romeva, that you and the whole fisheries committee have worked to ensure that this document was adopted at first reading by the spanish presidency to protect bluefin tuna.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would again like to thank the rapporteur and everybody for the very good interventions. i would like to repeat that this report will help us to have very good catch documentation, and i hope we will use it. i hope it will be a very useful instrument in our effort. the eu has to give the message that iuu fishing is unacceptable and that this applies to our vessels – to eu vessels – but it also applies to vessels under other flags. i would like to say that we will do all we can to persuade everybody that we have to cooperate in order to avoid this iuu fishing. we can do that. we have weapons and we will use them. concerning the general discussion on the bluefin tuna issue, i would like to say that we have to face the problem as it is now. we already have a scientists’ decision, and we have to respect it, but we also have the iccat efforts. we work there, we can use the iccat efforts, we can do our best. on behalf of the commission i can say that you can be sure that we will do our best to protect this species. i understand that you have a very difficult situation here, and we have the very difficult situation because the price of this fish is very high. we are talking about a lot of money in the international market, so it is not an easy battle. what i can say is that we can use all our weapons. i would like to remind you that underestimating our weapons is not the proper way forward. we have the weapons and we are going to use them. i have already used them, and you need only take notice of what my friend mr cadec said in his intervention. as regards the future, we will see after the scientific advice during november what will happen. we are doing our best to cooperate with member states and the council to reach a satisfactory decision.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i will just make a couple of final remarks. firstly, i want to be very honest and say that this has been a report which we could call 'easy'. there was a consensus from the start, from all the groups, and i think we must recognize this, in the sense that we all agree that there is a problem of control, that more control is needed and, above all, that we must be much more not only transparent but also forceful with those who do not comply with the rules. because this is detrimental to the tuna, first of all, and to those who do and want to do things right, secondly. i think that needs to be acknowledged and i welcome that. it was therefore relatively easy - very easy, i would say - to reach a consensus on parliament's report and, perhaps a little more complex, to reach agreement with the other institutions, but it was nevertheless possible, and i am pleased about that, for this document to be transposed and to become a reference in europe and, i would say, the world in terms of marking, traceability and, above all, transparency in terms of the activity of catching and monitoring or marketing bluefin tuna. another thing will be - and we shall see this in the coming months and years, if we have the chance - how we understand other measures which are also necessary. and here it is clear that we have very different views. in any case, i think that the next meeting of the iccaa will give us a little more insight into the seriousness of the situation, which we agree is serious. where we disagree is on how serious it is. and here's where it seems to have some nuances. how much we are willing to apply the precautionary principle and how much risk we are willing to take still. especially considering that no one can tell us exactly what the population situation is, because no one has gone down to count how many animals there are. so, we all clearly work with probabilities. but here it is also important to make another mention. i think what mr milana said about the control agency is important. we have had the opportunity to visit the agency recently and there we have seen not only how important and vital the work they do is, but also how necessary it is that they have the political support and the resources to do their job well. i think it is essential that the governments of the member states understand the fundamental role of this agency. we must support their work because it benefits not only the tuna, not only the sector that does things right, but also the environment and sustainability much more than today. so i thank all the groups, i thank the two institutions, commissioner damanaki, the spanish government - the president-in-office of the council - and in that sense, let us simply start working from today on the implementation of this report, especially - i insist - bearing in mind that, unfortunately, this will solve part of the problem, but not the fundamental problem, and this will require us to have many more discussions and many more commitments than we have made today.

in writing. − i am very glad the ep supported my proposal of report on such an important issue. the new bluefin catch document is a welcome and valuable addition to the system slowly being put in place to regulate the bluefin tuna fishery, but by itself, it is not going to save the species from collapse. after many years of over-exploitation, including large catches taken illegally by eu and other fleets, bluefin tuna is severely depleted. commissioner damanaki recognized this by supporting a ban on international trade in bluefin earlier this year at cites, which would have had the effect of significantly reducing catches, bringing them more in line with scientific advice. if the european union is to be consistent in its policy on bluefin tuna, then it must behave more responsibly at the next meeting of iccat, to take place in paris from 17-27 november. for many years, the eu used its very considerable influence in iccat to push for quotas that were far higher than scientific advice, while at the same time not putting in place strict monitoring of the fishery. as a result, quotas were sometimes exceeded.

in writing. − environmental problems with aquaculture are multitude. it can cause local pollution if farms are placed in poor sites or in too great a density; escaped fish can interfere with reproduction of local stocks (genetic pollution); high densities favour diseases and parasites that must be fought with antibiotics, vaccines, etc; there are animal welfare concerns over the conditions of the animals. probably the most important problem, though, is that for many species of farmed fish, including the most popular ones such as salmon, the farmed animals must be fed with fish - so we have the absurd situation of fishing to feed fish that are reared in cages. herbivorous species such as carp do not have this problem, though. fish accepted a number of our amendments that were intended to counter these points - to insist that european aquaculture must concentrate on herbivorous species, that depletion of wild fish stocks to feed farmed fish is not sustainable, that subsidies for aquaculture must be based upon environmental impact assessments.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission subscribes to the views expressed by honourable members in the various motions regarding the recent executions of 18 people in libya. the commission condemns executions as they are in contradiction with our values. we consider capital punishment to be cruel and inhumane, failing to deter criminal behaviour and representing an unacceptable denial of human dignity and integrity. the commission is particularly disturbed by the fact that these executions have taken place just weeks after libya was elected to be a member of the united nations human rights council. in this context, the eu, in conformity with the eu guidelines on the death penalty, has made a démarche towards the libyan authorities to express our condemnation and to remind libya of its legal obligation – contained in article 14 of the international covenant on civil and political rights, ratified by libya on 15 may 1970 – to provide all possible safeguards to ensure a fair trial. in this démarche the eu has also encouraged libya to establish a moratorium with a view to considering the abolition of the death penalty for all crimes. the commission is committed to continuing the policy of engagement with libya that the council has decided. in this context, the conclusion of the framework agreement between the eu and libya will provide the legal basis for establishing a regular dialogue and cooperation on all human rights issues. negotiations on the framework agreement are progressing well. the seventh round of negotiations took place last week in tripoli and the commission can report that good progress has been made, especially regarding political issues. in conclusion let me stress that the commission is fully aware that certain topics are problematic in relations with libya. nonetheless, the commission is committed to developing the eu-libya dialogue further on the basis of mutual trust in order to be able to address all issues in an open and constructive manner, including very sensitive ones as in this case. libya has shown its strong will to deepen relations with the eu. while considering this very positive, the commission intends to put these relations on the basis of a growing respect for fundamental values and rights.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's citizens are able to enjoy their holidays in the summer months. in fact, the maritime passenger transport and cruise ships have grown very significantly and are an essential factor of development and wealth in both coastal and port europe and inland europe. for all the entrepreneurs, the workers and, of course, the travellers in this important sector, the european parliament has good news today, because the agreement we have reached with the council, with the great help of the commission, is to establish a common framework of travellers' rights, such as those already enjoyed by air and rail travellers. this is an unacceptable shortcoming for a sector which is in the midst of modernisation and expansion. this agreement, which was concluded under the spanish presidency - to which i am particularly grateful for the efforts of the spanish presidency, the other permanent representations and, of course, my colleagues and the services of this house - substantially improves the rights of passengers, particularly those with reduced mobility, as the disabled associations have insistently asked us to do. on the one hand, the scope is widened, in line with parliament's initial position, that is to say, all vessels of more than 12 passengers are covered by this regulation, but a certain flexibility is allowed for small companies offering excursions, historic vessels, ferries carrying lorry drivers and carriers making short river journeys and who might have too many costs in the immediate implementation of this first provision. parliament has also succeeded in removing any mention of the possibility of being denied boarding on the grounds of disability, limiting it to situations where, for safety reasons, the safe transport of the person is endangered. the council also gave up the possibility of refusing boarding on health grounds, which was highly controversial since it was the first time that a passenger regulation made reference to health. the time for which passengers are entitled to compensation has also been improved from 120 to 90 minutes; a per diem of 80 euros per night has been obtained in the event of an overnight stay; from 120 to a total of 240 we have obtained double that amount; provision has been made for the obligation to place the burden of proof on the carrier in the event of exceptional circumstances which exempt him from compliance with his obligations, as well as the need to adapt equipment in ports, etc. we have also succeeded in reducing the maximum ceiling on the ticket for reimbursement, from the initial 40 euros to 24. it should also be noted that the regulation provides the flexibility necessary for the particularities of this mode of transport, which is more prone to delays due to bad weather, so that certain provisions, such as those relating to financial compensation for delay or accommodation, will be excluded from the obligations in the event of bad weather. finally, it should be noted that the agreed text requires the member states to set up bodies which, in addition to ensuring that this regulation is properly applied, are independent of commercial interests and can also generate a whole system of penalties, as well as deal with complaints from passengers who have been rejected at first instance in a body which carriers will also have to set up. we have also succeeded in this regulation in enabling the associations of disabled people and travellers to participate actively and we have also succeeded in encouraging a little bit the port authorities to become more involved in the decisions that are applied, so we have proposed that, wherever possible, the whole regulation should also apply to ports and not just to terminals, as the council proposed. i think we have also achieved - and this is important because it was one of the historical requests of disabled people's associations - that staff training and updating on that training should also be part of this regulation. and we've also secured the quick replacement of mobility equipment, in case it has been damaged during the journey, with a suitable alternative. finally, we have succeeded in reducing the time taken to implement it by one year. i therefore think that this was a good negotiation and i thank all those who have helped us to bring good news to european travellers for once.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i would like to thank all my colleagues and the commissioner and vice-president, mr kallas, for their kindness and encouraging words. i would like to make a few comments on what mrs lichtenberger said about ports. i think you've misread the text. it is true that we have not succeeded in including all ports - because there are some ports which are simply a jetty - but there are obligations for ports, for example, all new or renewed ports are obliged to provide all the accessibility and equipment, something which we have justly forced the council to remove from the clause in which it was excluded. annex ii, if you read it, mrs lichtenberger, you will see that it is precisely the obligations for assistance in ports and port terminals that it refers to. and we have also included, despite the council's reservations on several points, the port authorities, precisely so that they are increasingly aware of the needs of people with reduced mobility. so ports do have obligations. the ports are included and therefore it is not only the ships and the vessels but also the port terminals and the ports that have obligations. as regards the exceptions to flexibility, i am grateful to both mr kuhn and mrs wortmann-kool for their comments. i think we have made an effort to be flexible and to help small businesses in a time of crisis. i understand that mr cramer is angry because it is true that our interlocutors are mostly large companies, but because european associations, and that is why they are european associations, include small and large companies. the fact that our interlocutors are sometimes, or often, those representing large companies does not mean that small companies are not represented in european associations. i think we've made an effort to understand all of them. finally, i would like to thank mrs bilbao in particular for her support and solidarity in improving the rights of disabled people. i am particularly grateful to you for your emphasis on the whole issue of accessible formats, on the fact that the council has finally given up on the health issue - which i think was a risk that will have to be worked on in the future, but certainly not now - and also on all the reduction of deadlines and improvements. finally, i would like to thank all my fellow alternative rapporteurs and, above all, congratulate european passengers because we now have 24 months for the sector - vice-president of the commission. − mr president, firstly i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr dirk sterckx, for his efforts on the directive on reporting formalities for ships arriving in, or departing from, ports. this is a very important step: it is not merely a matter of formality. this directive simplifies administrative formalities for shipping services and will reduce costs for the economy and end consumers. moreover, it will make short-sea shipping more attractive. the directive is part of the action plan to establish a european maritime transport space without barriers, with the concept of extending the internal market to intra-eu maritime transport by simplifying administrative routines. indeed, maritime transport is subject to complex administrative procedures even when vessels ply only between eu ports and the cargo consists only of internal market goods. the consequence is that the intra-eu maritime transport of goods is faced with unnecessary extra administrative costs. an important issue raised during the discussion was a deadline for european ports to accept electronic transmission of port formalities. the compromise suggests 15 june 2015. we accept that the requirements for introducing a single window are stricter in the current text than in the council general approach. the commission is also ready to look into the need for a clear framework for the granting of pilotage exemption certificates in european sea ports. the commission will communicate its findings to the other institutions and will propose further action based on these findings. the commission also accepts the report on several other issues: possible extension of the directive to inland waterways; facilitation of intra-eu maritime transport in relation to ports outside the eu; collection of statistics; and updates of the technical provisions in the directive. to conclude, the commission supports the compromise reached by the rapporteur, mr sterckx, and the council presidency. this is a good and well-balanced compromise based on the general principles from the commission’s proposal.

the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the european communities' financial interests is a very important one. the committee on petitions' activity this year was marked by the change from the sixth to the seventh parliament, as you know, which meant a major change in the composition of the committee, since two thirds of its members are joining it for the first time. the report aims to provide a clear overview of the committee on petitions' activities during the year and, ultimately, a more precise explanation of what it means to petition the european parliament, as well as the possible outcome of the process, its achievements and limitations. in addition, this report examines the progress made in implementing previous recommendations aimed at improving the work of the committee and highlights the main future challenges in the light of the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, not only confirmed the right to petition the european parliament as one of the pillars of european citizenship, but also laid the necessary foundations for increasing citizens' participation in the decision-making process of the european union by offering citizens the opportunity to suggest improvements or additions to union legislation. in this respect, the committee on petitions is pleased to be able to cooperate, in accordance with rule 50 of parliament's rules of procedure, with the committee on constitutional affairs in the drafting of the report on the european citizens' initiative, which should be completed by the end of this year. furthermore, and in the same context as the treaty of lisbon, the committee on petitions of the european parliament should establish closer working relations with the counterparts of the regional and national parliaments of the member states, in order to promote mutual understanding of petitions on european issues and to ensure a prompt response to citizens at the most appropriate level. i would also like to draw the attention of honourable members to the legally binding nature of the charter of fundamental rights which it has acquired with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, and to underline the importance of the charter in enhancing the understanding and awareness of fundamental rights by all citizens. i am confident that all the necessary procedural measures will be taken to ensure that the institutional aspects of the european union's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms are rapidly identified. this is of the utmost importance, given the problem which the committee on petitions is facing on a daily basis with regard to the infringement of property rights in certain member states, since neither the commission nor parliament are in a position to take any legal action. i would also like to emphasize the excellent relations which this european parliament has with the european ombudsman. we particularly appreciate the efforts of the ombudsman's office to increase public awareness of its work and to identify and resolve cases of maladministration by the european institutions. in this respect, we support the ombudsman's idea of establishing an administrative code of conduct for the administration of the european union. we call for the development of an internet system that clearly indicates the different complaint mechanisms available to citizens and which means are most appropriate to their interests. this would require the creation of a single online information window. but not all of it was going to be positive. i would like to take this opportunity to protest against the constant practice, since 2007, of the dg for the presidency and the dg for communication, of registering as petitions what, in accordance with rule 201 (1) of parliament's rules of procedure, is not. i'm talking about the "not requests" calls. their treatment is an unnecessary waste of time, apart from the cost of dedicated staff. to make you aware of the importance of this point, i will give you just one fact: these 'no requests' calls account for 25% of all in writing. − the function of the paris convention on international exhibitions is to regulate the frequency, quality and procedures of international exhibitions falling within its remit. the main purpose of international exhibitions, as stated in the paris convention, is to facilitate the display of innovation and contribute to the education of the public. as it regulates aspects falling within european union customs legislation, a member state wishing to accede to that convention therefore requires eu authorisation. the european union itself cannot accede to the paris convention, as only sovereign states can be parties thereto. so far 24 member states, with the exception of latvia, luxembourg and ireland, have acceded to the paris convention and latvia has expressed its wish to accede to it. the purpose of the council decision is thus to enable the member states that have not yet acceded to the paris convention to do so, while respecting the exclusive competences of the european union granted by the lisbon treaty. the verts/ale group has followed the rapporteur’s proposal in consenting to the proposal for a council decision authorising the member states to accede to the paris convention.
in writing. − we greens have not been convinced that we should support the leinen proposal to consent to the council position on this issue. the fact is that on 19 february 2010 the commission published a proposal for a council decision to conclude, on behalf of the european union, the protocol on integrated coastal zone management (the iczm protocol) to the convention for the protection of the marine environment and the coastal region of the mediterranean (the convention is more commonly known as ‘the barcelona convention’; it was originally signed on 16 february 1976 and subsequently amended on 10 june 1995). the european union is a contracting party to the barcelona convention, as are all eu mediterranean coastal member states. under article 4(3) of the convention, the contracting parties must promote the integrated management of coastal zones, taking into account the protection of areas of ecological and landscape interest and the rational use of natural resources. however, personally i find the proposal weak: bearing in mind that we need at least 40% of protected areas, i do not see a strong position in that respect.
in writing. − although the parliament has backed the busuttil proposal to consent to the council proposal regarding the agreement between the eu and iceland and norway on the application of certain provisions of council decision 2008/615/jha and council decision 2008/616/jha, we greens found too many unanswered questions on how it would be implemented, so we have not supported that approach, and we have voted against.
in writing. - i consider the establishment of frontex (european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders) to be unacceptable. the migration issue requires a strategy against poverty and in favour of employment and peace, as well as a fair trade strategy by the eu countries as a significant contribution to the stability of the regions bordering the european union. in my view, the way the eu is dealing with the phenomenon of migration is a real disgrace for europe. the main exponents of this policy which criminalizes migration and abolishes the fundamental rights of migrants are the unfortunate shame directive and the work of frontex. member states are reducing their aid to cooperation and preventing developing countries from meeting the millennium development goals. i am against the fortress europe which uses migrants as cheap, precarious and unrighteous labour, and against the current repressive community policy on immigration.
in writing. − the aim of the proposal for a council decision which is the subject of this consent procedure is the signature and conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an arrangement between the european community, of the one part, and the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein, of the other part, on the modalities of those states' participation in the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union, called frontex. we greens did not see many problems there, so we voted in favour.

in writing. − in the context of the global financial and economic crisis, eu regional policy makes a contribution to the economic recovery plan by speeding up implementation of programmes under the cohesion policy. the policy of ‘pre-financing’ for programmes under the 2007-2013 cohesion policy resulted in immediate liquidity of eur 6.25 billion for investment in 2009, within the framework of the financing packages agreed with the member states. at the committee stage, green/efa amendments were adopted on: support by the financing instruments earmarked for objective 2 for bodies working for a social, inclusive economy; adding the protection of the environment and the potential development of renewable energy as areas where added value of eu interventions can be demonstrated; and taking appropriate action (short- and long-term measures) for urban regions and centres that present particular and significant social problems (high unemployment, marginalisation, social exclusion, etc.) which have increased owing to the impact of the crisis.
