rapporteur. − mr president, at the origin of this financial crisis are the national supervisors. our financial markets are integrated at a european level and in every country the main financial institutions are cross-border institutions, but financial supervision has remained only at national level. at this stage and with the huge crisis we are suffering, there are only two possibilities. we can reinforce the national supervisors or we can create european supervisors in order to adapt european financial supervision to the globalisation process. in this report i propose a closer link between the european central bank and the european systemic risk board. the president of the ecb will also be the chair of the esrb and represent the esrb externally. in my opinion, the european central bank has gained credibility and has become an institution of worldwide renown in this financial crisis. it has been recognised all over the world, including by some anglo-saxon experts, such as david marsh, the chairman of the london and oxford group. in my opinion, the european central bank is the only european independent institution that will have the moral and material authority to play an important role in future european supervision of both financial markets and financial institutions. to justify why a closer link between the ecb and the esrb is needed, we can see what is happening in other countries outside the eurozone. three weeks ago it was my pleasure to read in the financial times that mr george osborne, the uk conservative finance minister, has decided the biggest overhaul of city regulation since 1997. the uk splits the main financial regulator and gives more power and more clout to the bank of england. in the same direction that we are now proposing, the uk has abolished the english tripartite structure, formed by the bank of england, the financial services authority and the treasury. mr osborne said that it had failed to prevent the crisis because no one knew who was in charge. mr osborne will hand the bank of england full control for monitoring systemic risk in the economy as well as oversight of individual banks. finally, i completely agree with mr osborne when he argues that nowadays only independent central banks have the broad macroeconomic understanding, the authority and the knowledge required to make the kind of macro-prudential judgements that are required. this report was voted in the committee on economic and monetary affairs with a large cross-party majority, so i believe that, with these arguments, the uk conservatives will also vote in favour of my proposal at european level. to close my speech, this is not time for a debate on a second order reform. i know that state nationalism is now rising in the eu and i know that there is no consensus for such sweeping reform but this is our choice – jumping to a political and economic union or reverting to our insolvent nations. let me conclude by saying that, in my opinion, only a closer and stronger union can save the eurozone. (applause)
the commission's proposal for a regulation on the financial supervision of the european union is a very important one. its work, which formally began in september 2009 with the presentation by the commission of the legislative proposals following the de larosière group report, has deeper roots in this house. i would like to mention in particular the work of all the members of the european parliament who have been advocating for years the need for european financial supervision, and in particular those representing my group. when the council adopted its position under the swedish presidency in december last year, the main parliamentary groups received it as insufficient to address the shortcomings identified. the rapporteur was then able to reach a broad agreement in the economic affairs committee of the european parliament, which was materialized in the vote of 10 may. the next day the trilogues began. since then, a marathon of meetings has taken place: 18 under the spanish presidency and two under the current belgian presidency. very significant progress has been made in key areas where there are already important bases for the agreement: definition of objectives; consumer protection; the role of the authorities in the regulatory process; control of legality; the establishment of binding mediation; temporary product bans; the introduction of the concept of systemic risk and the strengthening of supervision related to it; the extension of the concept of 'stakeholder'; the non-abusive use of the safeguard clause; the voting system of the authorities, etc. in bringing this point to this house we envisaged completing the negotiating process by that date. we wanted to send a positive signal to our citizens and to the financial markets, to affirm our commitment that the authorities should be operational by 1 january and to support the conclusions of the european council in june in favour of a swift conclusion of the negotiations. we have been open to compromise until the last moment, but the technical, legal and political complexity of the file has not allowed a final text to be reached. the new presidency of the council has also expressly asked for time to align its positions with the prospect of an agreement at first reading. we need to continue our efforts as co-legislators, because this agreement is still possible. the rapporteur has therefore decided to vote on the text which reflects our commitment, endorsing parliament's ambitious mandate, but not to put the legislative resolution to the vote. we have therefore left room for compromise at first reading in the coming weeks. the omnibus directive, for which i am the rapporteur, introduces the new supervisory architecture into eleven directives of community sectoral legislation relating to banking and securities markets. this is not, therefore, an ordinary general review. there is a broad parliamentary consensus to do so by preserving the acquis communautaire, adapting comitology procedures to the lisbon treaty and updating the lamfalussy architecture in the area of financial services. financial supervision should be based on the existence of a set of rules, a single rule book at european level, and to achieve this, a key role for authorities in the development of technical rules, whether regulatory, by means of delegated or implementing acts, has been recognised in all sectoral legislation, in accordance with the lisbon treaty. and the commission has been given the necessary powers to ensure that it is adopted within the time limits. all competences and powers have been incorporated into sectoral legislation. i hope that the negotiations on this directive can be concluded satisfactorily.
the rapporteur. - madam president, cassandra had a gift: that of divining the future. she also carried a curse: that of not being heard. that's why troy fell. more than ten years ago, this parliament anticipated that a liberalization of the markets without at the same time setting up european supervisory mechanisms would end up with a crisis of the system. for a very simple reason: crossborder institutions cannot be supervised by national authorities whose jurisdiction extends beyond borders. they can only be supervised by european authorities. they ignored us and the crisis broke out. exotic products, unknown even to their creators, flooded the markets. nobody trusted anybody, nobody lent anybody, and credit dried up. the result: 23 million unemployed and 3.5 billion euro - a third of our production - committed to support the financial sector. so, what now? the council and parliament have been at odds until a few days ago. parliament has given up a lot to get an agreement, and so has the commission. the belgian presidency has shown good will. he asked for time. we're going to give it to him. but we are going to show today that parliament is united, that it has very clear ideas. that is why we are going to vote massively tomorrow on amendments which have been tabled jointly by the main groups in the house. the ideas which this parliament wishes to underline are several. the first is that the crisis will only be overcome when confidence is restored and transparency is restored in markets, institutions and products. and that will only be possible if there are credible, strong, independent and democratically controlled european supervisory authorities, authorities which do not simply docilely repeat the slogans emanating from their national governments. and what do you mean they're european? it means that they must have real power to prohibit the marketing of toxic products; it means that they must have real power to put an end to the regulatory distortions which hinder the functioning of the market; it means that they must have real power to oblige national supervisors to always act in the european interest. the national supervisors cannot be feudal lords invested with absolute power. the european authority must ensure that the law is enforced, that national authorities do what needs to be done when there is a threat of a pandemic and that they are able to resolve conflicts when the colleges of supervisors are unwilling or unable to do so. they must be able to force private institutions that are out of the game to do what needs to be done when national supervisors have ignored european guidelines. the second lesson is that within border institutions, there is a special, unique species: the so-called systemic institutions. one of the basic truths of capitalism is that when you do it right, you make money, and when you do it wrong, you lose money. that applies to everyone but the systemic institutions. when things go well, they make a fortune, and when things go bad, it has to be the taxpayer who runs to their rescue. there are only two solutions to the problem of systemic institutions, only two: either the supervisors in the countries where they operate are given more powers to control their solvency and liquidity, and that means abolishing the european parliament, or we have truly european institutions, which is what this parliament proposes. that means that the european authorities must keep a close eye on these institutions, because their ruin is the ruin of us all. it means that the european institution must be equipped with resolution and control mechanisms to stabilise the institutions in danger, if that is possible, or to liquidate them, if that is not possible. lifeboats are prepared before the crossing, never in the middle of a storm. and thirdly, we must force these systemic institutions to pre-finance, to provide funds to guarantee the interests of depositors, which is our main interest, and to pay the costs of the crisis when that happens. what cannot be is that the taxpayer has to pay for the broken dishes again. what can't be, given how much americans are quoted, is that main street is going to pay wall street's excesses again. ladies and gentlemen of the council, absent today - you have been very active this morning, calling on the telephone, and it seems that the storm has passed and we are calm and you are no longer here - i am sending you the same message through the commissioner. the council has asked for time. parliament has given it to him. but no one gets confused. it's not a sign of weakness. it is a sign of the strength of this parliament. the strength of the one who believes in what he says and feels supported by the citizenship, who backs him up. the council and the commission, which are doing a magnificent job, must use this time to forge a consensus in parliament on the european direction, towards europe. they must not use this time to try to forge blocking minorities against this parliament. for once, i ask the council to listen to cassandra. casandra are the speakers today. casandra is also michel barnier. those of you who aren't cassandra know exactly who i'm talking about. listen to parliament, seek a deal, say here what you said in toronto. don't say one thing here and another there. as the old castilians say, if the council does so, god will reward it and if not, he will demand it. god and this chamber.
opinion of the committee on constitutional affairs. - madam president, i believe that there are only two possible solutions to the financial crisis we have had: either we give more powers to the national supervisors or we create a european supervisor and give him powers. and i am glad, madam president, that at this moment the firm commitment, the political commitment of this parliament, and i believe with a great deal of agreement from all the political groups, is to european supervision. the committee on constitutional affairs will support and has supported all the institutional measures that go in that direction. at the moment, once that bet is made clear tomorrow, it seems to me, madam president, that the commission has a first-class role in the negotiations with the council. and in that negotiation, i think the key point will be whether those european supervisory authorities can go directly to the companies concerned at national level if the national supervisor does not intervene. so, commissioner, good luck in this task, which i believe is crucial for the future of supervision and capital, at the moment, for those who want more europe.

de larosière's proposal. a word on a subject which mr bokros and mr audy raised earlier about accounting standards. it is a question of that transatlantic calibration which i sometimes mention. i'm not worried about the mutual stimulation between americans and europeans. 80% of financial exchanges are currently taking place between the two sides. the rest of the world is here, between americans and europeans. i observe that president obama, the european leaders signed the agreements, made the decisions together at the g20. so we have the same road map. the last g20 was, in my view, more of a follow-up g20. it is important that we should show the same determination to implement what has already been decided and is far from being implemented. the americans have taken a different approach from ours, they have adopted a global package. now they'll have to open the drawers one by one to implement the decisions. we ourselves have a series of proposals, the ones that are currently being considered on the regulation of hedge funds and private equity, the one that has just been adopted with crd 3, the ones that will be, i hope, with supervision. as you know, brick by brick, week by week, we will put all the commission's expected proposals into effect at the g20. that is why i wanted, not to do the same as the americans, but to give you a comprehensive vision, so that journalists, businesses, markets, citizens and european and national parliamentarians can have a comprehensive and global vision, to put this whole agenda into a comprehensive and coherent document, which was adopted on 2 june last and which is now our road map. the americans have made some headway in some areas, but we are also going to take action on an extremely important point, namely the regulation of derivatives and short selling, starting next september. i think there's a real parallel between americans and europeans. we don't always have the same tools. we won't always have the same methods. our banking sectors are not alike. i would remind you that in europe banks finance between two thirds and three quarters of the economy. in the united states, the ratio is the opposite. we don't always have the same banking structures. we won't always have the same tools, but we have to achieve the same goals in parallel time. the only point, mr president, where we have a point of debate which can become a point of divergence is the point mr audy has noted, which is the extremely important one of accounting standards. we have a confident but not naive dialogue with the americans on this subject. i can conclude by thanking you for your speeches.
rapporteur. − mr president, i propose that we imagine for a moment what would have happened in europe with this huge crisis without the euro. in my case, i could argue that spain would probably have had a big corralito. the euro was created 11 years ago. creating a single currency was not an easy process and there were great speculative attacks on very important european currencies. however, i think that the benefits and advantages of the euro for the eurozone citizens are much higher than the costs associated with it. dear colleagues, now we are experiencing another european momentum; another european train – european financial supervision – has arrived at the train station and it is waiting for the european countries to jump on board. let me also say that we will not have another opportunity to rescue the financial sector if there is another financial crisis and we continue doing business as usual. i will not say ‘in the ecb we trust’, because i know that my colleague, sven giegold, does not like to mix economy and religion, but the further step towards a european financial authority increases the role of the european central bank in european financial supervision.
the european union has a special responsibility in the field of financial services, because it is the world leader in banking and insurance and the second in securities markets. our citizens are looking for a system of supervision that ensures the reliability and resilience of our financial services. and we cannot let them down. i think we should take our time and get a quick settlement. we could go further in three directions: first, to ensure the effectiveness of the authorities' decisions in emergency cases; second, to make clear our commitment to the priority of protection for savers by depositary institutions; third, to advance a european crisis resolution system. those who yesterday advocated self-regulation must now accept self-financing. citizens cannot be the ones paying the bills and the broken dishes in the next crisis. in the omnibus directive, there are three directions: the first is to adapt to lisbon; the second is to increase transparency by providing information on sanctions to the european securities and markets authority and ensuring that financial institutions provide the information necessary to ensure responsible investment; and the third is to ensure correlation tables in the transposition of the directives. i would like to thank the rapporteurs - my fellow countrymen, mr tremosa and mr garcía-margallo, my colleagues mr giegold and mr goulard, my colleagues mr peter skinner and mrs elisa ferreira - the alternate rapporteurs, those who tabled amendments, all those who contributed, the staff of the secretariat, the group managers and my assistants. they have done an excellent job, which has not yet borne fruit. i would like to say that i also acknowledge the work of the representatives of the presidency and the commission. but we do not have the vocation of cassandra in this parliament; we want to legislate and to have effective supervision.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the council must take note: if in six months they have spent their lives telling us that there was a mandate closed by the swedish presidency, we now also have a mandate. and since we are talking about cassandra, the important thing is not to prophesy the past, which is what the spanish presidency did, but to prophesy the future, which is what the belgian presidency seems to want to do. we have a consensus as strong as the council's, with the added advantage that the winds are favourable to parliament's position and not favourable to the old and anachronistic position which the council has held until the arrival of the belgian presidency. we have the advantage of incorporating proposals which were rejected, proposals which were in the de larosière report, such as the resolution mechanisms to which mrs ferreira referred. it makes no sense to set up a supervisor who can forecast the weather but can do nothing in the event of a shipwreck. we have the advantage of having anticipated things that other institutions have said later. when we talked about systemic institutions, we were told that there was no such animal species. the european council in march recognised its existence. when we talked about the taxpayer not having to bear the cost of the crisis and that funds pre-financed by the sector had to be set up to meet its responsibilities, we were told that this was premature, utopian or simply stupid. then the europe 2020 strategy, which was adopted by the commission, ecofin, the european council and the council in toronto, said so, and i do not understand why they do not defend it now. member of the commission. − the first part of mrs gutiérrez-cortines’ question refers to whether the procedure for the selection of the jti’s senior executive managers guarantees independence from the influence of large companies. the answer is ‘yes’. the procedure for selecting the executive directors for joint technology initiatives follows the guidelines for the appointment of heads of community agencies and joint undertakings. the guidelines are applied to all eu bodies and hence ensure that jti selection processes are fully coherent with those of other eu bodies such as executive agencies and regulatory agencies. in this way, the process for all eu bodies including jtis is based on competence and merit and guarantees equal treatment to all candidates. in this respect, as was prescribed in the guidelines, commission senior staff members were a majority both in the pre-selection committees and during the proceedings of the consultative committee on appointments. these are the only two steps of the procedure where industry was given a role in one way or the other, apart from the indirect role of industry representatives when they cast their vote in the governing board at the moment of the appointment itself, which is among candidates shortlisted by the commission. it is to be noted that the running and operational costs of all jtis are partially covered by industry, up to 67% in the case of eniac and artemis, the two joint technology initiatives in the field of nanotechnologies and embedded computer systems. this implies that their involvement was necessary and in keeping with the nature of jtis as public-private partnerships. the second part of the question asks whether in those selection processes the eu commitment to supporting smes is taken into account. the answer is that, generally, staff selection criteria for the day-to-day operation of the jti must be based – as mentioned earlier regarding the guidelines for appointment – on competence and merit. in this respect, the promotion of smes is an important political objective of the commission but may not easily translate into selection criteria for the appointment of staff covered by the eu staff regulations such as jti staff. the executive director and his or her staff are covered by professional ethics principles in the eu staff regulations and thus they are not allowed to defend or represent any specific interest, be it smes or large companies. the eu staff regulations foresee disciplinary procedures for breaches of this obligation. having said that, the regulations establishing the joint technology initiatives cater for smes. they contain provisions encouraging and promoting sme participation and representation at governing board level.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. we know that the itcs are common bodies and that they therefore have a selection procedure which must be respected. and we also know that the people elected should not come directly from the companies that are sitting on the board of directors. i'll give you a specific case. in the hydrogen itc with a budget of 470 million euros, you, in the european commission, have made a selection procedure which ended up with three people, and finally with one, who is an expert of the european commission who comes from the small and medium-sized enterprise and who, however, when i arrived at the board of the hydrogen itc i was replaced by a person who came from the large company, in particular toyota daimler. i think this case law completely contradicts the answer you have given me, which should be logic in relation to procedure. i therefore ask you, commissioner, to keep a close eye on the selection procedure.

member of the commission. − fair trade-type schemes – or ‘private sustainability assurance schemes’, to give them their proper, though rather cumbersome, label – have an important role to play in promoting development and informing customer choice. one of their biggest assets is that they are non-governmental in nature. as expressed in the commission’s may 2009 communication on these schemes, governmental involvement should be limited so as not to interfere with the dynamic nature of fair trade and the manifestation of consumer preference. i would also recognise that there is considerable scope for consumer confusion. that is why the commission is supportive of the efforts of bodies such as the iseal alliance, the international trade centre and unctad to provide more clarity on the sustainability criteria used for different schemes. in the commission, responsibility for fair trade-type schemes is shared between different commissioners depending on the initiative in question. thus, for example, the services of commissioners tajani and barnier have taken the lead in the preparation of the guide to socially responsible procurement. those of commissioner dalli lead on informing eu consumers, and those of commissioner piebalgs lead when it comes to projects in developing countries. dg trade currently plays a central coordinating role to ensure that eu policy initiatives are coherent and consistent with the 2009 communication, and i am prepared to maintain that coordinating role in line with the commitment taken by my predecessors.

member of the commission. − mr president, in march 2009, parliament voted on the novel foods proposal at first reading. many of the amendments that were carried have been incorporated into the council position that was adopted at first reading in march 2010. the council position maintains the principle of the need for pre-market authorisation for innovative products to reassure consumers that new production techniques are safe for humans and animals and respect both the interests of consumers and the environment. the proposed procedure would streamline and speed up the authorisation process through a centralised food safety evaluation undertaken by efsa, and would set precise deadlines at every stage of the process. it also includes an improved safety assessment to allow safe traditional food from third countries to enter the eu more easily. i am grateful for parliament’s broad support for the improvement of the proposal to streamline the authorisation procedure. turning to nanomaterials, i underline that the commission is considering the ep’s request for the systematic labelling of all food containing nanomaterials with a favourable disposition. however, before finalisation of the text, we need to come to an agreement on the adaptation to the new provisions of the lisbon treaty, especially those regarding the necessary adaptations of the definition of nanomaterials. i am confident that a balanced solution can be found so that the improved text can be finalised in a timely manner. regarding animal cloning, i share the importance that parliament attaches to this highly sensitive issue. as members will recall, i am committed to producing a report considering all aspects of cloning for food production by november 2010, which will be followed by legislative proposals if appropriate. i am committed to looking at all issues, especially those relating to the health and welfare of cloned animals during their productive life and natural lifespan. the impact that any measures on cloning would have on international trade is also a key aspect which will be addressed in this report. i will view the conclusions of this report with an open mind, in writing. at a time when inequalities are exploding and the unfairness of pay has become the norm in the financial world, i welcome the adoption of this directive as a first step towards capping pay and bonuses. we will continue to denounce these outrageous and abusive behaviours day after day, however, until we see action taken to reduce the gap between the low wages and the salaries of executives in large companies, by means of a european maximum income.
in writing. i voted in favour of the liotard report on novel foods because it excludes the sale of food from cloned animals from the rules for the authorization of novel foods. i believe that the european commission cannot continue to ignore the wishes of the citizens not to consume food derived from cloned animals. it is not guaranteed that the ingestion of these products does not pose a serious risk to health. cloned animals have high rates of malformations. we cannot allow the european commission to ignore this reality and endanger the health of citizens and the conservation of our ecosystem. i therefore believe that until it is guaranteed that these foods are not harmful to health, they cannot be allowed to be marketed.
in writing. − the vote on novel foods went very well. however, there was one downside: the amendment on the labelling of products produced from animals fed with genetically modified feedingstuffs was removed from the report. it was, remarkably, supported by a majority of meps (351+, 296–) but unfortunately the absolute majority (369) needed at second reading was not reached. as for the rest, the committee on the environment’s position was reaffirmed, with exclusion of foods derived from cloned animals and their descendants from the scope. before six months after the date of entry into force of this regulation, the commission shall present a legislative proposal to prohibit the placing on the market in the community of foods derived from cloned animals and their descendants. pending the entry into force, a moratorium should be imposed on the placing on the market of such foods.
in writing. − today’s vote on industrial emissions legislation is a step in the right direction for limiting the damage to our environment from industrial pollutants but it is regrettable that the final outcome falls short in key areas. though the new legislation brings some improvement, it still allows for too many exemptions. i am still dissatisfied by the final outcome which gives the all-clear to more air pollution by the oldest and dirtiest power plants. these power plants will be able to escape the rules for up to 12 more years. instead of rewarding good behaviour we are rewarding pollution, with european citizens paying the price. the aim of this directive is to ensure better protection of european citizens and the environment by obliging industries to limit their environmental pollution. i am disappointed that this weak compromise plays into the hands of those member states that rely on the most ancient large combustion plants. the eco-industry already employs more people than the car industry and this directive could have further promoted innovative, green industries. instead, the interests of the most polluting, out-of-date industries that have no real future were put first by a blocking minority in the council.
in writing. - i am very pleased that the european parliament has given the green light to a regulation banning trade in illegally harvested timber in the eu and introducing fines and other sanctions against infringers. the new legislation, agreed by parliament and the council, will apply from the end of 2012 and will contribute to the fight against deforestation and forest degradation. it will also give consumers more assurance about the origin of the wood in the products they buy. the new regulation, adopted by 644 votes to 25, with 16 abstentions, prohibits trade in eu timber from illegal logging and products made from it. it is estimated that 20% of timber products traded in the eu today are from illegal sources. until now, there was no explicit prohibition on trade in this raw material in the eu and therefore, even if the wood came from illegal logging, it could be legally traded on the european market.
in writing. − after two months of tenacious negotiations with council, the european parliament today voted on its amendments to the commission proposals for financial supervision. a broad coalition has made it clear that the parliament will only agree to the final package if ambitious rules for new european financial supervision are set. at the same time, the parliament has left open an opportunity for agreement by postponing the final first reading vote until september. the council must now grasp this chance to overcome its own lethargy and walk over the bridge that parliament has built. after 20 trialogue meetings, council has not presented a compromise offer, whereas parliament has submitted a comprehensive proposal. hence, the negotiations have turned out to be disappointing. the council negotiators have failed. as a european institution, the council must not leave itself hostage to national interests and must be prepared, if needed, to vote by qualified majority to reach agreement with the parliament. the european parliament will only agree to a first reading agreement in september if the european supervisory authorities are given real powers.
in writing. - the european parliament has just adopted a directive restricting bonuses in the banking sector. from january 2011, only 30% of the bonus can be paid in cash and at least half will be paid as shares or capital available to the bank in case of difficulties. in addition, variable incentives should be proportionate to wages. the rules adopted today also strengthen the capital requirements for banks. this means that, two years after the global financial crisis, these new rules will transform the culture of bonuses and end the incentives that drive bank managers to take excessive risks. a culture of high-risk, short-term bonuses is damaging the economy and it's the taxpayers who end up paying for it. since the banks have failed to introduce reforms, we are the ones doing the work for them.
in writing. − i support the strategy adopted by the rapporteurs on the so-called financial supervision package. meps have just voted in plenary on amendments to the texts setting up the eu's new supervisory architecture, tabled by the four main political groups (epp, s&d, alde, greens). the ep has decided not to vote on a legislative resolution in order to leave open the possibility of a first reading after the summer recess. the message is clear: parliament is willing to negotiate, but it is united in its view that the european authorities must be equipped with sufficient powers to prevent future crises and to strengthen the single market. the ball is now firmly in the council's court to come forward with the necessary compromises. this gesture is a final endeavour on the part of the rapporteurs to help the new belgian presidency – whose efforts to date we applaud – move the member states to a more satisfactory position.
in writing. − i supported the report led by ferreira according to which we, the ep, request the commission to submit to parliament by 31 december 2010, on the basis of articles 50 and 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, one or more legislative proposals relating to an eu crisis-management framework, an eu financial stability fund and a resolution unit, following the detailed recommendations made in the annex thereto, taking into account initiatives taken by international bodies, such as the g-20 and the international monetary fund, in order to ensure a global level playing field and based on a profound analysis of all alternatives available, including an impact assessment.

the author. mr president, today is a day of congratulations: first of all to the spanish foreign minister, mr moratinos, who has managed to bring several cuban political prisoners to spain, or is about to do so; also to guillermo fariñas, the political prisoner who, with his hunger strike, his tenacity and his sacrifice, has achieved the release of these prisoners. and, above all, speaking now of the subject which brings us here, i would like to congratulate the council and the commission on the start of negotiations for a major trade agreement, which is also political and of cooperation, between the european union and mercosur, which was decided at the madrid summit on 18 may. contrary to what is said, this parliament has repeatedly supported such negotiations, both in the delegation for relations with the mercosur countries and in the delegation to the euro-latin american parliamentary assembly (eurolat) and in the plenary during several legislatures. we are talking about what can and should be the largest trade agreement in the world, which will bring development, prosperity, progress and employment to 800 million people by dramatically increasing the exchange of goods, commodities and services between the two regions. agriculture is only one part of that macro-agreement. the negotiations must seek balanced agreements, but not with the mentality of protectionism, which is the enemy of development and well-being; european protectionism and protectionism also in some of the mercosur countries. moreover, industry and services account for 97% of european gdp and agriculture for only 2.1%. the fears must therefore be dealt with in their proper terms of proportion and justification. the next eu-brazil summit, on 14 july, should therefore serve to give impetus and speed to these negotiations, the conclusion of which is all the more important given the economic crisis we are suffering, and to the solution of which this agreement will contribute.
mr president, we all welcome the release of political prisoners in cuba. however, in the chapter on congratulations i have missed a congratulation to the catholic church and, above all, to the role played by this parliament, which has been key in the resolute defence of all those in cuba who are fighting for their freedom and dignity. as regards the mercosur issue, some clarifications are necessary. as commissioner de gucht has explained, the commission presented negotiating directives for the conclusion of an association agreement between the european union and mercosur, which were approved by the council and this parliament. the negotiations have been stalled for six years and it is clear that, on the horizon of the summit of heads of state and government of the european union, latin america and the caribbean, there has been a relaunch of these negotiations, with the support of this parliament too. the aim at the moment is to reach a balanced agreement which takes account of the interests of all the sectors of the european union as a whole. i do not see why certain sectors or interests should be harmed in this negotiation. it has not been for ten years and it need not be in the future. this will depend on the firmness of our negotiators. in any event, if that were to happen, it is clear that the commission would have to arbitrate compensatory measures for the sectors concerned. this has been done with third countries, with acp countries and in the latest agreements with the andean community. and if it has been done to these countries, all the more reason to do so in defence of the european union's banana producers.
mr president, the relaunch of the eu-mercosur negotiations is part of a positive context which makes it possible to restore the dialogue on trade relations. the talks have only just been resumed and it is good that today's debate serves the commission to take note of what we think. even if the european union has offensive interests in sectors such as wine, olive oil, meat products or preserved fruit and vegetables, it is logical to assume that they will in no way compensate for the impact that is expected on community livestock and agricultural production, such as sugar or cereals. i ask the commission to work towards a balanced agreement as a whole which takes account of the sensitivity of certain productions. it should include the necessary mechanisms to prevent malfunctions and strict control of the sanitary and phytosanitary quality levels of imported products. another important issue is to avoid overlapping results with doha and the european union doubling its agricultural concessions. that said, i join the criticism of the restrictive measures adopted by argentina against certain european products and i hope that the commission has acted firmly to resolve them promptly.
mr president, this report is a response to the frustration and helplessness of the community fisheries sector. this sector, commissioner, does not demand protectionism, but what it does demand at this stage, given the history of ignorance of those responsible for the dg trade, is that it not be further undermined. we therefore support in particular the request in mr cadec's report that the negotiations on the fisheries chapters be transferred from the competence of dg commerce to that of dg maritime affairs and fisheries, as is the case with agriculture, since we are also dealing with particularly sensitive products, the exemplary case being tuna. and as regards tuna, we have a glaring example in the agreements with papua new guinea and fiji, through the repeal of the rules of origin, which will only favour our main competitors - thailand and the philippines - no matter under what conditions. mr commissioner, are you aware that, in addition to drowning the community sector, your policy is also leading papua new guinea into a dynamic of low-quality job creation and zero sustainable development? do you know the complaints of ngos in the area about child labour, unsanitary and unhygienic conditions in factories, the disastrous environmental impact on the madang coast and illegal fishing? is it your responsibility to prevent it?
mr president, commissioner damanaki, commissioner de gucht, thank you for being here to discuss a very important report on the import regime. the fisheries sector is an important issue in which two fundamental aspects must be emphasized: we are not self-sufficient and there is often unfair competition, so we must ensure fisheries in europe and we must avoid unfair competition. i would like to say to the commissioner for trade: fisheries cannot continue to be regarded as a 'non-sensitive product'; it cannot continue to be governed by the amna rules; it cannot be a product like industry; it must be a 'sensitive product' and it must be governed by the rules of the wto and the fao. we cannot therefore be sustainable, we cannot guarantee the maintenance of species and we cannot make a real market action if we do not consider fisheries as a 'sensitive product'.

in writing. - i have again voted against the swift agreement for the processing and transfer of european banking data to the united states under the pretext of the fight against terrorism, because i consider the us claim to be unacceptable and to be an attack on the freedoms and rights of european citizens. with their proposal, the most conservative forces intended to hand us over to american interests, without regard for the security or privacy of citizens. the european parliament cannot allow the civil rights and freedoms of europeans to be violated under the pretext of the fight against terrorism.
in writing. − the adoption of the new swift agreement by a majority in parliament is a blow for the negotiations on a binding protection of fundamental rights in international security cooperation. there were some improvements to the first draft, but there is still fundamental criticism of the massive data transfers without initial suspicion and the over-long data retention periods. the grand coalition of conservatives, social democrats and liberals has therefore accepted lower standards than the existing principles of the rule of law and is risking a regulation that is in breach of eu law. we greens have therefore opposed the new agreement and, as a progressive force, aim for stronger privacy protection and the principle of the rule of law in transatlantic cooperation. as parliament’s rapporteur for the comprehensive data protection agreement planned by justice commissioner viviane reding, i will personally work with the us administration and the us congress on binding rules in this field. it is therefore really sad to see that the european parliament has weakened its influence on the united states by accepting the swift agreement today. a real change towards binding fundamental rights protection in the fight against terrorism requires greater courage and effort.
in writing. - i voted against the report on the european external action service because i believe that it institutionalises the militarisation of the european union. i have voted to express my absolute rejection of the negotiating procedure for the creation of the eeas, in which the rapporteurs and catherine ashton have given in to pressure from some member states and have completely forgotten the rules of democracy. the eeas is going to become a sui generis institution that escapes the basic control mechanisms of any democratic system. i believe that we must ensure that the european parliament, the only democratically elected institution of the eu, and the national parliaments have not only budgetary but also political control of the eeas. my group is particularly concerned about the important military orientation of the eeas and that the bulk of the civilian component of european foreign policy is placed under the umbrella of the european security and defence policy. more specifically, in all matters relating to development cooperation and conflict resolution. for these reasons, the gue/ngl, committed to the eu's values of peace and demilitarisation, does not support the creation of the eeas.
in writing. − parliament’s approval paves the way for a more coherent and effective european foreign policy that better meets citizens’ expectations. a better service could have been possible, though. we regret that ms ashton, the commission and a number of national governments did not have the guts to embrace a more ambitious solution. we support the compromise because parliament managed to improve ms ashton’s original proposal considerably. a strong human rights structure, safeguards for development policy and against renationalisation of community policies, strengthened democratic scrutiny, a more transparent foreign affairs budget and gender balance in recruitment are cases in point. the deal is not flawless, however. its weak points include the unclearly defined crisis management structures, the lack of permanent deputies for ms ashton and the limited scope of the eeas’s consular services to citizens. much will now depend on how the compromise is implemented – the ball is therefore back in the court of ms ashton, the member states and the commission. they must work together, create a common esprit de corps and overcome divisive competition.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution on kosovo because it encourages the five member states which have not recognised kosovo's unilateral independence to do so. the group of the european united left - nordic green left has always been against the unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo because it is an act contrary to international law. on the contrary, we remain committed to a return to dialogue in a mutually satisfactory manner, based on un security council resolution 1244/99, in accordance with international law, as the only possible way of achieving peace and stability in the region.
in writing. - on behalf of the spanish delegation to the epp group, we wish to state that the reason for our vote on the resolution on the process of european integration in kosovo is that this resolution treats kosovo as if it were an independent state in a state of complete normality, without taking into account that the status of this territory remains highly controversial in the international community, that an advisory opinion of the international court of justice is even pending, and that kosovo has not been recognised by five member states of the european union, including spain.
in writing. − the european parliament today sent a clear signal that the future of independent kosovo lies in eu integration. this is a signal of encouragement for the government as well as the citizens of kosovo. in addition, it is a clear request to the five eu member states which have not yet recognised kosovo as a state to promptly do so in order to raise the effectiveness of our support. a clear majority of meps rejected a further discussion on the question of kosovo’s status, bearing in mind that a statement from the international court of justice (icj) is due in july. with this resolution, parliament is in favour of starting talks on visa liberalisation as soon as possible. the people of kosovo should no longer be refused the freedom of travel which the eu will have probably granted to the other states in the region by the end of the year. my resolution calls for this necessary step to urgently be implemented to free the kosovars from their regional as well as international isolation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on albania because it confirms parliament’s support for albania’s european prospects, once the country has reached a level of political stability and reliability and the copenhagen criteria are fully met. it notes the progress made in the reform process, stressing that further substantial efforts are needed in terms of the consolidation of democracy and the rule of law and of the sustainable development of the country. the resolution welcomes the adoption of the proposal on visa liberalisation and calls for the introduction of a visa waiver for albanian citizens by the end of 2010. it stresses the importance of the separation of powers and the respect for an independent judiciary, calling for particular progress to be made on the issue. the issues of corruption and organised crime, and trafficking in human beings are among the most worrying situations in the country on which the resolution takes a stand. the report also deals with minority rights, the roma, trade union rights and the social situation, womens’ rights and consultation of the government with civil society on the draft laws and reforms undertaken. it encourages the development and use of renewable energy, public transport and environmental legislation.
in writing. − i welcome the adoption of this resolution, especially because it welcomes the progress made in respect of the judicial system, but underlines that implementation of the reforms is still at an early stage; takes the view that judicial reform, including the enforcement of court decisions, is a key prerequisite for albania’s eu membership application process, and underlines the importance of the separation of powers in a democratic society; stresses that a transparent, impartial and efficient judiciary, independent of all political or other pressure or control, is fundamental to the rule of law, and calls for the urgent adoption of a comprehensive long-term strategy in this field, including a roadmap for adopting the necessary legislation and implementing measures; calls on the opposition to be involved in the drafting process and to give full support to the reform of the judiciary; stresses, moreover, that the judiciary needs to be provided with sufficient funding to enable it to operate effectively throughout the country; looks forward, therefore, to new assistance initiatives from the commission and welcomes, in this regard, the recent inauguration of a serious crimes court in tirana.
in writing. − i welcome the adoption of this resolution mainly because it calls for a substantial increase in eu humanitarian aid to the people affected by the recent violence in southern kyrgyzstan, as well as for comprehensive use of the instrument for stability, and because it stresses our belief that a new level of eu engagement in southern kyrgyzstan will be necessary in the longer term as well; reiterates parliament’s call to the commission to prepare proposals for a reallocation of funds under the development cooperation instrument designed to put the eu in a better position to give a sustained response to the new situation in kyrgyzstan; and maintains that a focus on human security is essential in the eu’s central asia policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint resolution of all the groups in parliament on hiv/aids because it deals with important elements of this problem, such as the defence of universality in access to public health services for all citizens. the resolution also calls on governments to fulfil their obligation to make public health care available to all citizens. the resolution also protects the sexual and reproductive health rights of hiv-positive people. it also stressed the need for appropriate funding for research into new preventive measures, including vaccines.
in writing. at the dawn of the next international aids conference in vienna from 18 to 23 july 2010, i would like to join the resolution adopted today in sending a strong message to national governments. indeed, new laws are urgently needed to provide affordable and effective anti-hiv medicines, including antiretrovirals and other safe and effective medicines. i would like to remind you that only 23% of hiv patients are aware of antiretroviral treatment in europe and central asia. for example, the baltic states are the countries in the european union that most need to implement policies to combat aids. i therefore call on the european union agency for fundamental rights to collect more data on the situation of people living with hiv/aids and to ensure that people living with hiv/aids continue to have the right to a full social, sexual and reproductive life.
in writing. − the joint resolution was adopted as negotiated with 400 votes in favour and 166 against, despite the ppe group requesting split votes on sexual and reproductive rights, which it does every time. it also shows that the ppe group is divided on the issue. i am happy with the result, especially because all our considerations related to sexual and reproductive rights are in.
in writing. - unfortunately, the joint resolution contains positive references to the european security strategy and the common security and defence policy which both i and my group reject. however, because of the great importance of the convention on cluster munitions (ccm) which has been adopted by 107 countries, i and my group, the gue/ngl, also endorse the joint resolution on the entry into force of this convention and the role of the european union. i believe that the joint resolution can be seen as a step towards banning cluster bombs, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − with an overwhelming majority, the european parliament has sent a strong signal against this perfidious threat to humans in war and crisis areas. thousands of people continue to be affected by cluster munitions to this day: almost exclusively civilians, and in particular many children who frequently confuse the bomblets with balls and toys. thus, the european parliament took the only possible position on this indiscriminate and inhumane weapon: a united ‘no’ to cluster munitions in europe and throughout the world. the european parliament demands that all member states and candidate countries which have not yet signed or ratified the international treaty to ban cluster munitions should do so as soon as possible, preferably by the end of the year. we greens were successful in our demand that the countries which have not yet been named, should be named – allowing civil society to apply pressure where it is needed most. estonia, finland, greece, latvia, poland, romania, slovakia and turkey have yet to sign and ratify this treaty. bulgaria, cyprus, the czech republic, hungary, italy, lithuania, the netherlands, portugal and sweden have signed but still have to ratify the treaty in their national parliaments.
in writing. - the current common agricultural policy provides support for a speculative, off-the-shelf industrial production system which benefits large farms rather than small producers. the decoupling of aid favours large landowners and endangers small farms and family farming. despite the failure of the lisbon strategy, the eu has not changed its economic policy. it is not about food security, but about competitiveness, which only benefits the large multinationals. i believe that the agricultural sector must be considered as a strategic sector in the european union. i therefore believe that a thorough reform of the cap is necessary to guarantee small farmers access to aid, land, seeds and water and thus support a social, productive and sustainable agricultural model.
in writing. − the greens/efa have been able to include an important number of amendments which focused on environmental and social conditioning of direct payments, measures against climate change, a broader and more inclusive approach to rural territorial development and fair income for farmers. we also have been able to introduce a clear distinction between different levels of competition in farming and marketing of food products and supported a clear statement to replace the current basis of historical yields and income by payments to farmers by an inclusion of the principle of ‘public goods’ in direct payment calculations. thus, the adoption of this report is highly satisfactory.
in writing. − this report was originally a defence of a protectionist stance with respect to imports, mostly in the belief that eu fishermen should have preferential access to the eu market, except when they cannot catch enough, in which case eu processors should be able to import. since our belief is that too much international trade leads to over-exploitation and depletion of fish stocks as countries seek to increase their exports, there was a good basis for common ground. indeed, we got a good number of our amendments adopted, the most important one pointing out that, even if international trade in fish products can lead to increased food security in developing countries, it has also led to increased fishing in order to supply the export market, which can exacerbate stock depletion. other amendments stressed the need to strengthen resource management and fisheries surveillance, and the need for responsible consumption, and noted that fish supplies come from a wild natural resource which is limited in quantity, which means that there is a limit to how much fish can be caught, exported and consumed.

ahead of us, and as mr bové said, these are issues which are not only at the heart of the current situation but also on the agenda for decisions to be taken in the immediate and medium term, particularly in the context of the reform of the common agricultural policy which we are preparing. i share most of the concerns expressed in this report. i think that the functioning of the agri-food chain really needs to be improved. all the actors involved have everything to gain: consumers, the retail trade, the processing sector and in particular - as mr bové said - farmers, who are probably the ones who have the most difficulty in obtaining a fair share of the revenue in the distribution of income within the chain. the commission has recently taken a number of initiatives in this respect. i want to recall a few of them. first, the high level group on the competitiveness of the agri-food industry made a number of strategic recommendations. mr bové takes up analyses and enriches some of these proposals in the report he is presenting to us. these proposals will be complemented by a high-level forum, recently launched by commissioner tajani, which will address issues such as contractual relations, logistics and competitiveness. as far as price transparency is concerned, it is indeed considered to be essential to the proper functioning of the sector and it is an area where there is work to be done. the food price monitoring instrument has been set up, as you know, in the framework of eurostat, but it needs to be refined. it will be refined so that the information obtained can actually be useful to the actors in the agri-food chain, to farmers and consumers and to all other actors as well. the commission recently published a report on market surveillance in trade and distribution, which recognises that 'structural inefficiencies' in the food supply chain could contribute to 'asymmetric transmission and price rigidity and unfair contractual terms for primary producers'. other i would remind you that interested parties are invited to submit comments on this report by 10 september this year. this report falls within the competence of the european commission's directorate-general for the internal market and, on the basis of this report, we will no doubt have new information to consider measures to correct this asymmetrical transmission of prices which causes structural inefficiencies in the chain. the commission is also preparing legislative proposals to improve the quality of agricultural and agri-food products. we have already had occasion to speak on this subject, including in this house. the commission will present the legislative package on this issue by the end of the year and we will present proposals, among other things, to support local and regional initiatives for the marketing of food products, to give producers, especially small producers, agricultural producers targeting direct sales markets, short-distance markets, the opportunity to better identify their products on the markets and thus also to help consumers to make better choices when they buy. in the context of the proposals for the common agricultural policy after 2013, i will also ensure that instruments for the promotion of agricultural products can be improved. i think that this is an area in which, precisely in the new context, the european commission can do more to help producers, the agri-food chain, to promote products better on the european market and on the world market. i would also like to point out that the high level group on milk has presented its report. following this report, the commission will present a legislative package for the dairy sector by the end of the year - i remind you - which will address, among other things, issues related to the negotiating powers of producers and their possibilities to organise themselves to better negotiate their contracts, and to contractual relations in the sector. i also intend to address the question of the role of inter-branch organisations in the proper functioning of the chain, particularly in the dairy sector. on derivatives and commodities and the speculation issue, the european commission - and here i am working very closely and in agreement with my colleague commissioner barnier - is putting the finishing touches to a general legislative proposal. other proposals will follow in the context of the review of the directive on the market in financial instruments. we also need to go further in analysing the distribution of value added across the agri-food chain; this is a point to which i attach particular importance. as i said, the asymmetry of bargaining power between producers and the rest of the agri-food chain has kept a strong pressure on the margins of producers in the agricultural sector. so i think that there are things to be done here too, and an issue to be addressed as part of the reform of the cap. i would also like to stress in this connection that the competitiveness of the agri-food chain in the european union cannot be ensured at the expense of certain components and i think that the actors in the agri-food chain must be aware that too much pressure on raw material producers, on farmers, risks harming the whole chain, its economic power and its representativeness in the european industrial sector. i thank you again for the report presented by the european parliament. this is a very useful contribution to our common objective of improving the functioning of the agri-food chain. i shall be very attentive to the debate and vote on this report.

the next item is the commission statement on products derived from cloned animals in the food chain.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i am glad to have been offered this opportunity to set out where the commission stands on the sensitive issue of animal cloning for food production. first, i should underline that there is no evidence of any food safety concerns regarding foods obtained from cloned animals. there are, however, some animal welfare issues that require further consideration. such concerns are nevertheless likely to decrease over time, as the technique evolves and improves. there is, of course, an ethical dimension to this issue, which, i should add, lies outside the eu’s legislative remit. other considerations in the general debate on this issue are consumers’ rights to know about production processes, and the likely trade implications of taking measures in this area. the most important issue for the commission is to assess the need, feasibility and proportionality of possible measures to regulate the use of the cloning technique and of cloned animals and products. naturally, i am fully aware of parliament’s position on the use of cloning technologies for food production in europe. honourable members would like to see a ban extended to the offspring of cloned animals. the commission position is that foods from cloned animals should not be put on the market without prior authorisation, as they are considered novel foods, and indeed are currently covered by the novel food regulation. it is worth adding that, given the value of cloned animals, it is highly unlikely that they would be used directly for food purposes. the situation with regard to the offspring of cloned animals is, however, rather different. such animals cannot be distinguished from those of conventional lineage. this aspect also has to be taken into consideration in any line of action the commission may propose. turning to the current position, the commission acknowledges that the novel food regulation is not the appropriate legal framework for addressing all aspects of the cloning issue. in particular, the production and marketing of products other than food – such as ova, sperm or embryos – cannot be covered by the novel food regulation, which deals exclusively with the pre-market authorisation of food products. as honourable members will know, we are currently putting together a report which will cover all aspects of the use of cloning for food production. that report will be made available in november. it will serve as a useful basis for future discussions among the institutions. i look forward to continuing discussions with both parliament and the council with the aim of reaching a successful agreement.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, thank you also, commissioner, for the explanation you have given us on the cloning of animals for food use. we agree, both parliament and the commission, that the novel food regulation was not the framework for dealing with this issue. we agree and that is why it has been taken out of the scope of that regulation. we all know - at least that is what all the scientific committees say - that meat from cloned animals and their offspring meets all the requirements for food safety. only here i see a problem, and that is that it is impossible to distinguish whether a meat comes from a cloned animal, from a descendant of a cloned animal or from an animal that has not been cloned. therefore, labelling and traceability - which is essential - must be used to ensure that the consumer is informed. the consumer has a right to know and wants to know whether the meat he is eating, whether he knows it is healthy or not, comes from a cloned or non-cloned animal, because because of the animal welfare issues you have explained, or for ethical reasons, he may refuse to eat it. but in this situation i ask myself a question: the production and consumption of cloned animals is probably banned in europe, especially the production. we are hereby prohibiting our producers from using a technique which is a new technique, which is a good technique for the reproduction of animals and which, moreover, can generate profits because logically an animal is cloned when it has very special characteristics, as has been done in spain with the brave bulls. and we're going to ban it? are we going to make sure they can't have that technique in their hand? because then our farmers, our cattle farmers will lose competitiveness. and it would be very good if we could ban the import of meat from cloned animals and their offspring from other countries into europe. but are we going to ban it? we can't ban it. the world trade organization is not going to accept that we ban it. so we are going to have the absurd situation that our farmers are not going to be able to use a new technique that is going to enable them to be more competitive and yet we are going to be consuming, labelled or unlabelled, those foods within the european union. that is what concerns me, and i think we must find an explanation. why are we doing that? why are we going to stop our farmers from using that technique, and then bring in that food from outside because we can't stop it being imported?
member of the commission. – mr president, i am not surprised that this issue has attracted so much attention and debate and i thank all of you for expressing your views. the various points which have been raised show the need for a deep understanding of these issues so that we can take informed and proportionate decisions. as i said in my opening statement, the commission plans to adopt later this year a comprehensive report setting out the key issues which contribute to the cloning debate. i hope that this will serve to add clarity to this complex issue and will prove useful as a basis for the institutional debates and discussions that will follow. i emphasise that an improvement in the current situation can only be achieved through consensus amongst all eu institutions. this debate has been going on since january 2008, and i look forward to us making progress together on this issue, with the ultimate aim of agreeing on a practical way forward which will serve us well in the years to come.
the debate is closed. written declarations (article 149 of the regulation)

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this is a very important debate and i thank you, mr simpson, for having called it. i want to recall two or three things before going a little further in my answers. firstly, as i said earlier and as everyone, objectively, must recognize, this reform, this controlled opening of postal services, was not done in secret, or in haste, or by chance, but with regular democratic validations and the support of all governments. many of you have played a very important part in this: mr simpson you are one of those, mr markus ferber is another, and i could name many more. we're here now. it's a gradual process. there have been - as my services reminded me - some 20 sectoral studies. mr. de jong, there was no rush or secrecy. mr. tarabella, there was no forward leak either. things are done gradually and in stages. that's the first point. secondly, i know what is in the treaties and in the texts. mrs auconie recalled a very important word: i fought as one of the drafters of the old constitution and the new lisbon treaty - i was european commissioner at the time, in charge of institutional reforms - to put the words 'territorial cohesion' in the treaty. and it wasn't easy. they're words that mean something. as in the lisbon treaty, there are new words on the security or protection of public service missions. these are words which i attach importance to, beyond and in addition to my personal convictions, and i would like to summarize them in one sentence: i do not believe that europe is simply a large free trade area. europe is not just the big market. it is a common space of economic, social and human life. and i returned to the european commission with this conviction. it will remain attached to my action throughout the five years during which i shall have the honour of being in this position. that's what's in the treaty. i have not forgotten it and i will remind anyone who has forgotten it, if necessary. and then there are the texts of these directives, ladies and gentlemen. i do not think, frankly - and i say this to mrs wils and others - that a moratorium or a brutal blockage of this development would be helpful. this would, in my view, create damaging insecurity for businesses and for users and overall it would be irresponsible. but having said that, having confirmed that the process will take place, we have a duty to check that it is carried out correctly and in accordance with what is written in the texts of the directives and in the treaty on european union. mr bach and mrs auconie spoke of the universal postal service; there are important words in the texts that should strengthen universal service provision. there are many mechanisms that provide this benefit and we must check that they are used; this is the case for the compensation fund, designations under public procurement and other instruments. those are words i don't forget either. the inclusion of working conditions is also included as an essential requirement to be taken into account in the authorization or approval of postal operators. as regards social protection - mr de jong, mrs durant and mrs serracchiani have raised this issue - it is clearly stated in the third postal directive that the member states have instruments in their labour legislation to counter any social dumping and it is up to the member states themselves, in compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, to find the right approach to ensure this correct level of employment and social protection. i could give you many examples of phrases and words which are so much in demand from the member states, from companies and from the commission, under the control of your parliament and the council. i would also like to say a few words on a subject which concerns me, because i have been elected for 20 years from a rural and even very mountainous area, where we know the importance of public services for the most isolated or the most vulnerable people. mr gallagher has raised this issue, as have mr fernandes, mrs auconie and mrs harkin earlier. as regards rural areas, i would like to point out that if the member states do not comply with certain minimum requirements, the commission will use all the instruments at its disposal to ensure that the member states provide these basic postal services, particularly in rural areas under this territorial cohesion. i see that we must move forward, not run forwards, but make sure that what is stated in the texts, in the treaty, is respected. that is why, mr president, the stages of evaluation, study, reporting and, where appropriate, corrections must be used well. mr el khadraoui, mrs ticău and mrs wils referred to the first studies. i confirm that we will be conducting a first study this year - mr el khadraoui, at the end of this year - which will provide all stakeholders with an analysis of the latest developments in the postal markets and will also cover the most recent trends in employment. we will not stop there: there is the formal report we have to present to parliament and the council in 2013, when the whole directive will have been put in place by all the member states. and then there is this user dialogue group, in which you will participate, as will the trade unions, as will the companies and as will the users themselves, who will hear the group of regulators and who will review the evaluation studies provided by the commission. ladies and gentlemen, in conclusion - and i say this to mrs thun und hohenstein, mrs durant and others - i attach as much importance as you do to the fact that these directives are implemented correctly, without penalising citizens and users. i will attach as much importance as you do to the objectivity, the accuracy, the honesty of the evaluation studies. and since i am speaking of sincerity, i quote mr simpson: 'we must be fair to europe'. that is why these studies and the publicity we will give them, the debates we will create around these studies - especially in this user dialogue group - are important. i will be very keen to see that we are fair to the european union and the decisions we have taken together. when we talk about jobs in the postal services, when we talk about the quality of distribution, when we talk about territorial cohesion, when we talk about social protection, what is the result of european decisions? what is the reason for the decisions of the companies? what is the result of the political decisions of governments? we must say who is responsible for what and not make the european union responsible for everything that happens on the ground. that is why i want to finish this debate and evaluation. and that is why, mrs durant, ladies and gentlemen, i will personally chair the setting up of the user dialogue group, to demonstrate the sincerity and the willingness of the commission in this area which is at the heart of this great market, as a common economic and social area, which i love and for which i am one of the responsible.

in writing. − i welcome the important vote, today, on a resolution that draws attention to and expresses its concern at the devastation of the river jordan, and the lower jordan in particular. it calls on the authorities of all the riparian countries to cooperate and rehabilitate the river jordan by drawing up and implementing policies which focus on achieving tangible results in the areas of domestic and agricultural water-demand management, water conservation and the management of sewage and agricultural and industrial effluents, and on ensuring that an adequate quantity of fresh water flows into the lower jordan. it welcomes the cooperation among israeli, jordanian and palestinian local communities facing similar water challenges in the lower jordan area and calls on israel and jordan fully to honour commitments made in their peace treaty concerning the rehabilitation of the jordan river.
