madam president, asylum is a precise, defined legal concept which has nothing to do with a readmission agreement. the agreement with pakistan is a community instrument integrated in the framework of the fight against illegal immigration and not in the field of international protection or asylum. the purpose of the agreement is clear: the readmission of pakistani nationals who do not fulfil or no longer fulfil the conditions for entry, presence or residence in the territory of a member state, or of third-country nationals or stateless persons who hold a visa or residence permit issued by the pakistani authorities and who have entered the territory of a member state illegally from pakistan. respect for fundamental rights during the repatriation process must be ensured by requiring compliance with the rules of international law, in particular the principle of non-refoulement and the european convention on human rights. the measures contained in the agreement will apply only to persons who are in the territory of the union irregularly, without affecting those others who have been granted asylum or whose application for international protection is pending. i believe that we cannot and should not mix up different issues which could prevent the formalisation of a fundamental agreement in the development of the common immigration policy of the european union. so yes to the deal, but with the demand for guarantees from pakistan.
mr president, i think that in the year of biodiversity we have talked a lot about the tragedy that is happening, but very little about solutions. i believe that society needs solutions, new ways of approaching the problem. firstly, the division of europe into biogeographical areas would have to be translated into a specific policy, because the problems of different parts of europe are not the same. so we should have a micro-policy dedicated to biodiversity because, precisely, biodiversity is local. secondly, it is appalling that we should turn our backs on all measures concerning the soil and the abandonment of agricultural land when it is precisely the trophic cycle of animals that requires a detailed study of each area. and that's not done. what is not known is that in many areas, planting certain trees has more birds, planting certain plants also has more insects. experts acknowledge that the lack of insects is the great tragedy of biodiversity loss, especially in relation to birds. there is no mention of the problem of soil, of insects and of the organic richness of the soil. it seems a crime to talk about soil in europe. and finally, i want to say that owners are essential. the committee has rejected an amendment i tabled on stakeholders. but, well, if we have birds or animals, won't the farmer who plants the plants where they come to eat have a say? won't the habitat owner have a say? won't the farmers have a say? this kind of ideological dictatorship must be ended in europe if we are to achieve a better biodiversity.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the member states are not able to meet the requirements of the treaty. in the winters of 2005-2006 and 2008-2009, the supply cuts in the north and east of the union became a real nightmare. the harshness of the last few winters in europe has made it all the more necessary for us to do everything in our power to avoid similar situations in the future. the union's energy supply is largely dependent on external sources, and diplomacy can do much in this strategic field. we are all aware of the commission's efforts in this area - which we value and appreciate - but we need to have more directly effective mechanisms. we must bear in mind that in the supply crises we have experienced, the rules of the national markets and the lack of interconnections prevented fully satisfactory aid to the member states concerned. the regulation we are about to vote on is intended to be a firm step forward in solving this problem. we have been trying to make progress on this issue for a long time, overcoming the difficulties arising from the different national views, and the negotiations have been long and laborious. the agreement we are voting on today shows that the member states have moved beyond their partial positions to accept a much more european approach. once it is adopted, we will have a really powerful instrument to increase the security of gas supply in the union as a whole. the regulation was adopted unanimously by the committee on industry, research and energy, following the successful conclusion of the trilogues with the council. i would like to take this opportunity to thank all the alternative rapporteurs for their excellent work - which is reflected in the final text - and the members of the committees who contributed their views and whose amendments were incorporated into the text in significant numbers and importance. i would also like to thank the european commission for its valuable support to the co-legislators and to acknowledge the generous cooperation of the spanish presidency of the council, which kept us informed at all times of the state of play of its work. this regulation ensures the safety of each and every european citizen, who will now be better protected in the event of a crisis. in addition, some flexibility is given to member states to include additional protected customers such as public services. but the legitimate zeal of a member state to protect consumers in its national market must be balanced by an obligation of solidarity towards the citizens of the other member states of the union. the regulation imposes an obligation on gas supply companies to supply protected customers in the event of a crisis for a minimum period of 30 days without interruption. the member states will also have to build or renew their own infrastructure in order to further integrate the internal energy market and limit the presence of energy islands. one of the most important achievements of this regulation has been to impose reverse flow on all member states' gas interconnections, respecting the criteria of need and cost-effectiveness. the reverse flow will allow, with short-term investments and at an acceptable cost, an unprecedented diversification of supply in europe. a tangible example is the yamal gas pipeline, which supplies poland, the czech republic, slovakia and germany via belarus. another achievement of parliament is the important role given to the commission, which has the power to veto specific measures if it considers that they may jeopardise the security of supply of other member states. the commission will also play a decisive role in coordinating member states during crises through the gas coordination group. this regulation offers a real solution to a real problem: the regulation strengthens the security of gas supply and requires all market players to work together to deal with any acute supply problems. the correct and efficient functioning of the market, the building of interconnections and the diversification of suppliers and routes are the best defence against future crises. mr president, the regulation on the security of gas supply represents a profound qualitative change, whereby the member states abandon purely national schemes in order to enter fully into an ambitious european vision. it is true that two crises of pernicious effects have been necessary to awaken the community consciousness of some, but attrition is welcome if its consequences are analogous to those of constriction. finally, mr president, this regulation is a historic milestone towards the security of gas supply in the union and is a clear proof of the goodness of our great project of integration. the correct and rapid application of this regulation will send a very strong message to our suppliers and, in most cases, to our friends, that the union, as far as gas supply is concerned, is no longer governed by the slogan 'save yourselves' but by 'all for one and one for all'.

the following is the joint debate on the report by linda mcavan, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards pharmacovigilance of medicinal products for human use, regulation (ec) no 726/2004 laying down community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use and establishing a european medicines agency (com (((2008) 0664 c6-0515/2008 2008/0257 (((cod)) (a7-0153/2010), and the report by linda mcavan, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards pharmacovigilance, directive 2001/83/ec, laying down a community code on medicinal products for human use (com ((2008) 0652-0614 (cod)) (com (2008) 0602-065) 2008/06-06 (cod))
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, i would first of all like to highlight the work of the rapporteur, mrs mcavan, not only in substance but also in form, because she has worked in collaboration with all the alternative rapporteurs. i would also like to thank the experts from the spanish administration for their contribution to this agreement. the purpose of this european union pharmacovigilance system is to strengthen surveillance, transparency and communication in relation to the safety of medicinal products once they have been placed on the market, especially with regard to their risk profiles and the adverse reactions they may cause. the creation of the european pharmacovigilance committee, which will assess and make recommendations to the european medicines agency on safety issues that may arise with medicines placed on the market in the european union, is noteworthy. the solution reached for the notification of suspected adverse reactions to the eudravigilance database by both member states and marketing authorisations is very important. eudravigilance will be the only source of information, but at the same time the competent authority of the member state where the adverse reaction is suspected to have occurred will be informed, and this is very important. it is also worth noting that consumers will be able to report any adverse reaction and, in this regard, the creation and management by the agency of a european portal on the safety of medicinal products, which links to the portals of each member state, will help to improve the knowledge of citizens on the safety of medicinal products they consume. finally, we must not forget that, since pharmacovigilance plays a fundamental role in protecting public health, the adoption of this directive and this regulation will make a major contribution to that protection by improving not only the existing procedures but also the coordination of action between the various member states.

president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to take note of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the commission proposal for a regulation laying down the multiannual financial framework for the period 2007-13. i would like to say at this stage that i will be happy - and it will not be a surprise - to give you or to give you again the council's opinion on this matter. i would like to remind you that the council considers that the so-called lisbon legislative package in the budgetary field, of which this regulation is part, should be limited strictly to a technical implementation of the consequences of the lisbon treaty. in other words, the transposition of the current multiannual financial framework into a regulation should be nothing more than a transposition of the existing financial perspective. the commission proposal is exactly in that direction and the council does not therefore wish to discuss a revision of the multiannual financial framework at this stage. that said - as you will have understood - our positions are quite different, but i am convinced that in the coming weeks and months we will reach agreement on this regulation, at the latest, in particular during our negotiations in the context of the budgetary conciliation which is to be concluded at the end of november.

the next item is the commission statement on the european strategy for the economic and social development of mountain areas, islands and sparsely populated areas.
mr president, commissioner, if we are to achieve the objective of territorial cohesion, which is introduced in the new treaty, it is necessary that all the territories of the union should be able to enjoy the same rights and freedoms. we must therefore be very proud of the agreement reached in this parliament to promote the adaptation of european policies to the particular needs of islands, mountainous areas and sparsely populated areas so that these regions can develop their full potential and compete on equal terms. and in this connection i would like to emphasize something very important: at present some island regions do not have funding for crossborder cooperation projects simply because they are more than 150 km away. this is an irrational and unfair criterion which aggravates the isolation and which we propose to abolish. ladies and gentlemen, as the president has very well said, i live on an island in europe and i know firsthand that insularity has a cost. it is our duty as legislators to help to alleviate it. and as the commissioner has rightly pointed out, article 174 of the treaty gives us the opportunity to do so.
mr president, commissioner hahn, for the first time in the history of european integration, the treaty of lisbon incorporates the regional dimension and territorial cohesion as a defining objective of the union. i am speaking in this debate as a member of the european parliament from an island territory, the canary islands, which is covered by article 174 of the treaty in its specific reference to island territories, as well as by article 349 because of its status as an outermost region. but i am aware that, in addition to their territorial fragmentation, the islands, as they are always the external borders of the european union, pose a particular vulnerability to the union's energy, transport, infrastructure and, above all, internal and external security strategies in the face of threats, in particular against illicit trafficking. i therefore call for strong support for this resolution and, above all, for its translation into concrete policies - which must fill it with content and which we cannot go into in detail - and, in particular, for its transfer to the financial perspective for 2014-2020: that there be a budget that is up to the objectives and that financially supports the ambition of making the citizens who live and reside in the union's island territories citizens with full rights, with equal rights and opportunities with respect to citizens who reside in the continuous territory of this great area of integration which is the construction of europe.
mr president, i should like to begin by thanking all those who have signed this motion for a resolution, which we in the group of the european people's party (christian democrats) and in spain, the country we represent, welcome very warmly. we have the legal framework, we have the treaty of lisbon - the third paragraph of article 174 - we have territorial cohesion, which is the new pillar of this treaty, and we therefore have the legal bases to get on the road and help these regions - islands, mountain areas or depopulated areas. in the case of mountain areas - as has already been said here - there are more than 90 million inhabitants; in the case of islands, 21 million people live on islands, specifically in 14 countries; and many millions more live in mountain areas. all these regions share very similar problems in the areas of culture, education, transport and the environment. in particular, there is a disadvantage that unites us all, namely the disadvantage of transport. i come from the balearic islands, where the additional cost of transport has been estimated at 20%. this is certainly having an impact on our industry, our agriculture, our strategic sectors, our tourism and, in short, on the whole business sector, on the whole business fabric. and so it affects our competitiveness. so if we look at resources, like drinking water or soil, which is limited, or raw materials or energy or living space in these areas, we will see that they undoubtedly lead to a phenomenon of scarcity and lack of economic diversification. we therefore call for the new financial perspectives to take account of the specific features of these territories and for us to move - as has also been said here - from words to action, and this should be translated into a budget and thus into greater territorial cohesion.
mr president, keeping the population in sparsely populated areas is the best guarantee for their conservation. the strategy mentions the word development, but i want to emphasise three principles: first, the business models that generate development in these areas must be geared to profitability and the quality of production, and new activities linked to the low-carbon economy are the way to boost them. secondly, the social economy is the most appropriate mode of enterprise to link these populations in shared projects concerning their well-being. thirdly, people living in these areas must have access to a level of public services, health and education, as well as transport and telecommunications infrastructure, comparable to that of the rest of the population. better to invest in this than in production subsidies. that is what i want for the basque country, and, commissioner, this will only be possible if europe has the regions and local governments, if it clearly defines the objectives of the funds, if it assesses their impact and if it takes account of the different realities.
mr president, mr commissioner, issues such as unemployment, rural development, agriculture, fisheries, transport, the promotion of renewable energy and environmental protection are essential for our islands, mountainous regions and sparsely populated regions. we need an integrated and coordinated strategy with the aim of contributing coherently to its development. these areas have great potential for economic and social development which we cannot afford to lose. at the same time, to make this possible, we must compensate for the disadvantages arising from their particular geographical and demographic situation. in this respect, a necessary measure in the framework of regional policy is the removal of some of the limits to participation in crossborder cooperation programmes, such as the requirement that there be a maximum distance of 150 kilometres between crossborder regions, which hinders greater cooperation between island regions and with maritime border regions.
mr president, commissioner, to speak of territorial cohesion is necessarily to speak of islands, of mountain regions and also of the outermost regions. it is to talk about their problems and their difficulties, their natural handicaps and their structural handicaps. but it's also, and fundamentally, it's about talking about how we can remove the barriers that are holding them back, it's about talking about strategies to turn those disadvantages into opportunities. improving connectivity, a proper neighbourhood policy and stability in policies and in the structural funds are issues that we must tackle without any complexes, and all this on the basis of two major premises: territorial cohesion and the principle of solidarity. there are those who don't believe in strategy. i do, and this resolution should be a proof of this parliament's commitment to these regions and of the commission's demand that it should take political decisions which take account of the needs of these vulnerable territories and whose problems are manifested most sharply in times of economic crisis such as the present one.
mr president, i am very pleased that the european council has dealt with the union's external action. we are in a new world, with economic multipolarity and increasing political multipolarity with a small number of important actors. furthermore, the challenges are global. no country can face them alone, not even the eu. as the president of the commission said a few days ago, in the global world size does matter. the european union must be one of those actors. i therefore regret the vote in new york last week on strengthening the union's position at the united nations. it's very troubling what happened. i think it is very good that summits with the other major players should be carefully prepared in future. we have to discuss with them - in addition, of course, to the meaning of their vote on 14 december in new york - important bilateral and multilateral issues. among other things, it is about governing globalisation, adapting the institutions born after the second world war and strengthening more recent forums, such as the g-20. and in all this i think it is necessary to consult the united states. we share many values and interests with them. i trust that the summit on 20 november will be well prepared. ladies and gentlemen, thanks to the new instruments of the lisbon treaty, the union's external action will have more continuity and coherence. but alongside the union's internal strength, the political will of the 27 and, in particular, of its most important members, to act together is also essential. this process of conjunction will inevitably be long and difficult. but it is necessary if we are to avoid europe's irrelevance or what has already been called the advent of a post-western era.
president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is with great pleasure that i am returning to you to deal once again with financial supervision, since we had the opportunity to discuss it following the last ecofin meeting, the legislative package on supervision now being put to the vote in parliament. it is a set of texts that sets out a particularly important reform in the union and responds to several challenges. the first challenge - the president-in-office has just spoken about it - is the response to the crisis. the decade that is ending has seen the implementation and deployment of the lamfalussy architecture in all financial sectors. the committees of overseers have, in a sense, made their first weapons there. they have contributed to the development of european financial legislation and to a process of gradual convergence of prudential supervision. this process was an important and positive first step towards a european approach, but in the light of the crisis it must be admitted that this process did not prove ambitious enough in the end. it has not prevented or contained the financial crisis, nor coordinated rapid and effective responses on the ground, particularly in cross-border cooperation. that is why we are seeking to set up a european operational systemic risk committee, with the full administrative support of the european central bank, which, under the leadership of its president, is fully available to work on the implementation and establishment of this committee. i have no doubt that jean-claude trichet will bring all his competence and authority to bear, including in the follow-up to any warnings or recommendations made under his presidency. to the same end, we also want stronger, more responsive supervisory authorities, much better equipped to prepare community technical standards and ensure their full implementation, including in times of crisis. these authorities will have the legal means to enforce compliance with the standards on financial institutions in the event of a failure of a national supervisory authority. they will help to establish a genuine european supervisory area, which is essential for strengthening the internal market. they will thus be involved in the functioning of the colleges of supervisors and will help to settle any disputes between national authorities, while leaving the day-to-day conduct of prudential supervision to the latter. let us not be afraid of words, the establishment of these authorities is a historic agreement, as some have already pointed out on several occasions in this house. the belgian presidency made this its main priority in the area of financial markets, but also in a global way. make no mistake, we are thus continuing to build an original model of supervision - i will come back to that - but we must also take account of the evolution of supervisory structures in our main partners. this is the second challenge: to show that the eu-27 is capable of reforming its financial supervision structures without being pushed back by the united states in particular. with the larosière report in february 2009, which was very well received by the european council, the debate in europe had started on promising paths, but we had to make these hopes of reform come true. the united states has meanwhile embarked on a major overhaul of its supervision with the passing of the dodd-frank act. by voting today, as i hope, in favour of the legislative package, which is the fruit of a year of examination, negotiation and cooperation between the various institutions, the european parliament will be proving that the european union is not lagging behind and that it is also a leader in the reform process supported by the g20. but you can only be a true leader in the long run. we must not only vote today on this historic resolution, but also make our new system work and evolve. this is the third challenge. on the one hand, we are aiming for a model of microprudential supervision that is largely decentralised, where the authorities support and coordinate national supervisors without replacing them. on the other hand, we also want a system which is constantly being strengthened rather than being replaced. with the european systemic risk board, we will establish a key body for macroeconomic debate and decision-making, including at the transatlantic and even global level. with the european supervisory authorities we will have effective actors in risk prevention and management, if we are to give them the capacity to carry out their work. this is partly the case with the omnibus i directive, on which parliament is called upon to give its opinion today. but other legislative measures will have to follow as part of the revision of existing texts. it is on this point, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, that i would like to conclude. we are now at the end of a crucial first stage and, while hoping for a positive result from your vote just now, i would like to thank in particular the chairman of the econ committee, mrs bowles, the various rapporteurs of parliament, mrs goulard, mr garcía-margallo, mr skinner, mr giegold, mr sánchez presedo and their fictitious rapporteurs, and commissioners rehn and michel barnier, who are present in this house, and of course all their collaborators. we have had fruitful exchanges, obviously constructive, which have led to the package of amendments put to the vote today. but i hope that the determination to achieve that inspired us will continue to drive the negotiations on the next texts, which will complete and modernise this system even further. on behalf of my successors as president of the council, i believe i can commit myself to this in the coming months and, in the light of the recent negotiations, i am confident that this will be the case. i hope that we can come up with new agreements soon - particularly on investment funds - and that we can together, with commissioner barnier, support a whole timetable of actions to implement new legislation.

madam president, commissioner barnier, minister reynders, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the commitment to adopt the financial supervision package at first reading with a large majority. european supervision was an old aspiration in the construction of europe, an indispensable instrument for advancing financial integration, making monetary policy more effective and improving competitiveness. it was also a pending subject to put a stop to financial hypertrophy and to correct the gap between global finance and national supervision. the present crisis has confirmed the inadequacy of the market and of national solutions. the deficiencies in regulation and supervision identified must be corrected. in our case, supervision is a priority in financial reform because, if european regulation has been weak, supervision has been non-existent. european supervision lays the foundations for a comprehensive, thorough and credible reform. this first transnational experience is a step towards a consistent system of international financial supervision. parliament has worked together to make the package a triple focus: more balanced, reaching the safety and solvency of financial institutions, financial inclusion and the protection of consumers, depositors and taxpayers; more prudent, to respond to systemic risk, to act in emergency situations and to be able to temporarily ban toxic products; and more sustainable, fostering competitiveness, internalisation of costs and the prospect of a european crisis management system based on contributions from financial institutions. the omnibus directive enables the authorities to be put into operation by integrating them into sectoral legislation, specifying their powers and detailing rules for their operation, increases transparency in the exchange of information and cooperation, and at the same time sets a deadline for the reform in the legislative implementation process to be completed by 1 december 2012 and for transposition to be carried out with correlation tables. i would like to end by thanking all those who have made this package possible. today we are offering the first fruits, but this commitment marks a turning point in the evolution of finance and european democracy, because democracy is to legislate and to supervise, to ensure that laws are effective. so it has been shown that if we want better finance we need to go the way of more democracy.
madam president, the president of the european central bank will automatically become the president of the european systemic risk board for the next five years. this is not a minor issue. it visualises that the ecb is really implicated in the financial supervision of the european financial markets and institutions. it also means that mr trichet, who is also accountable in his hearings in this parliament, will also have to answer questions relating to financial supervision, not only questions relating to price stability. with this reform, the president of the ecb will risk his reputation and his credibility in achieving effective financial stability in europe. thanks to this reform, doing business as usual will be more difficult for the financial institutions that have generated this crisis. it will benefit future generations of european citizens.

in writing. we abstained on this report because the gains made in protecting human health and the environment have been cancelled out by gifts to industry which endanger the functioning of the european chemicals agency. it is acceptable that all biocidal products may eventually go through the centralised procedure. but this becomes unacceptable if the time limits for scientific evaluation are drastically reduced while their financial resources are reduced. we cannot want to do much more, faster and cheaper without compromising the quality of the work. this vote shows the true intentions of the right and the centre-right: a 'light' assessment for all biocidal products, with direct access to the entire internal market at the expense of the health of the population. the small consolation is that the sovereignty of member states to restrict or prohibit the use of biocidal substances will be respected - it is up to them to ensure a high level of protection.
in writing. − the european parliament today adopted legislation creating new eu financial supervisory authorities (for banking, insurance, pensions, securities and markets) and a european systemic risk board (esrb). today’s vote not only establishes eu-level financial supervision, it also represents a landmark for the creation of a new eu financial architecture and stronger regulation of europe’s financial markets. europe-wide regulation is the only viable response to the financial challenges we face and to preventing a return to financial chaos. this underlines the relevance of the eu at a time when renationalisation is raising its head. the supervisory authorities will be more important than originally foreseen and have real teeth due to the insistence of the eu parliament. a cross-political alliance of meps worked to ensure the authorities were given real powers in the face of opposition from some member states that refused to acknowledge lessons from the financial crisis. unfortunately, it seems parliament will have to continue to fight to ensure the new authorities are able to provide meaningful supervision. this means ensuring that the new authorities are sufficiently staffed and that they will have direct supervisory powers over market infrastructure (such as central counterparties and trade repositories). the greens are already working with the other main political groups to this end.

president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have the honour, once again this afternoon, of speaking on behalf of the high representative, lady ashton, and not on behalf of the council, as the table indicates. the european union and the united states attach great importance to the fact that their citizens can move easily from one side of the atlantic to the other. this mobility can be greatly facilitated by the possibility of making these trips without prior visa and without fees. however, while us citizens can travel to the schengen area without first obtaining a visa, the same cannot be said for eu citizens. thus, four member states are still excluded from the us visa waiver programme: bulgaria, cyprus, poland and romania. on the other hand, we can be glad that greece was recently included in this programme, on 5 april. this is a good result for the commission, which is making every effort to ensure that all member states benefit from the exemption programme, and for the successive presidencies which have been working to make progress on this matter. the commission has therefore produced a report every year since 2006 on all third countries which maintain the visa requirement for our citizens, in breach of the principle of reciprocity, since the european union attaches great importance to the existence of full reciprocity in this area. if the union exempts certain third countries, it is only right that they do the same for our citizens. moreover, for reasons of security which we understand well, the united states decided to introduce, at the beginning of 2009, an electronic pre-registration system. this system should only be used for passengers who are from a country that benefits from the visa waiver programme and who are travelling to the north american territory. since 8 september, each of these passengers has to pay an amount of 4 dollars which has been set to cover the administrative costs generated by the implementation of the esta. this is in addition to the ten dollars that these same passengers already have to pay under a law on tourism promotion. to this end, an agency has been charged with developing tourism and is financed to do so by a fund fed by the payment of this ten euro tax. in the light of these latest developments, you have asked the commission to take a position quickly. as early as december 2008, the commission reported on whether or not an esta should be considered equivalent to a visa and, at that time, provisionally concluded that it should not be. as soon as the final rules on esta have been published by the north american authorities, the commission will present its final report on the subject. it is clear that the payment of the said tax will be an important element in its assessment. the report will be taken into account by the council, which will then take the necessary measures, including any recommendations it deems appropriate. as you will have understood, we must deplore the introduction of this additional tax and the presidency shares the concerns expressed by parliament on this subject on several occasions and in particular in its resolution of 22 october last, in paragraph 18 in particular. and while this may seem small at first glance, it is worth remembering that it is due for each traveler, which can sometimes prove very costly for families. this policy therefore seems to me to be contrary to the stated wish of the united states to facilitate mobility between the two continents and will be a real obstacle to european citizens wishing to travel to the united states. i would like to conclude by confirming to you that the presidency will do everything in its power to help the commission to achieve full reciprocity of the visa exemption with the united states. thank you for your attention.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would also like to thank mr chastel for his remarks and for offering the council’s help, because in an issue as important as this one, the support of the council is absolutely crucial. regarding the position of the commission on the esta fee, i have to underline that it was immediately following the publication of this fee on 6 august that my colleague, commissioner malmström, issued a statement in which she expressed the understanding that this decision is taken in accordance with the travel promotion act’s obligations, but regretting very much the introduction of the fee. the commission made very clear its concerns that this fee is inconsistent with the oft-repeated commitment by the united states to facilitate trans-atlantic mobility and that it will be an additional burden for european citizens travelling to the united states. the eu has raised its serious concern vis-à-vis the us congress and the us administration on numerous occasions during the process of passing the travel promotion act. numerous démarches were made by the commission, both with the council presidencies and with third countries. in its démarches the commission also criticised the fact that the fees apply only to travellers under the us visa waiver programme and that therefore it is discriminatory. moreover, it seems peculiar that foreigners are requested to pay for promoting tourism to the us, as this may possibly lead to less, and not more, travel to the united states. the commission is currently examining further possible measures that could be taken vis-à-vis the united states in the framework of the eu reciprocity mechanism. the commission will issue formal comments to the us in the framework of the public consultation launched by the us on the interim rule. a final assessment of the present esta will be issued once the final rule on esta is published in the usa federal register, taking into account any possible changes. the commission has requested that this issue of concern be discussed with all member states at the upcoming justice and home affairs council on 7 and 8 october. subsequently, the esta fee will be raised at the next eu-us jha ministerial in december. the commission will, of course, continue to keep parliament informed at all stages of this process and on the démarches undertaken. minister chastel also reiterated the importance of equal treatment on the part of the united states vis-à-vis all eu member states in relation to the visa obligation. here i would like to remind you that significant progress has been achieved in the visa reciprocity mechanism over the last two years. further to the commission’s efforts to achieve full reciprocity with the us, eight more member states have joined the us visa waiver programme – seven member states at the end of 2008 and greece in april 2010. the commission continues to raise with the us at political and technical level the importance given by the eu to the admission of the four remaining eu member states – namely bulgaria, cyprus, poland and romania – to the visa waiver programme as soon as possible. i can assure you that the commission, in cooperation with the council and the high representative, will insist on putting this issue on the agenda of any future eu-us meetings.
i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. but it is necessary for this parliament to take note of the fact that a decision has been taken by the united states. this decision is contrary to the will of the transatlantic dialogue to continue to make progress in strengthening not only trade but also social and human exchanges in all their dimensions, based on mutual trust and reciprocity. we cannot accept the discriminatory application of a tax which clearly contradicts the promotion of such exchanges, which creates dividing lines between the member states of the european union and directly affects citizens, and which, moreover, contradicts the european attitude towards the united states and its fellow citizens, which has not only always been respectful of the will to strengthen human and commercial ties, but has always favoured the dimension of transatlantic mobility in relations between citizens of the two hemispheres. so i think it is very important that this parliament sends a clear message that it expects the commission to defend the european position vigorously and, if necessary, to enforce the reciprocity clause, which is obviously not good news for the transatlantic dialogue but would send a clear message that we are not prepared to accept, simply, the lack of reciprocity in promoting the human and social exchanges that take place through the link between european and american airlines, not to mention, obviously, the economic impact this would have on the serious crisis already affecting air transport on both sides of the atlantic.

president of the council. − the symposium entitled 'international symposium - enhancing partnerships between fisheries and scientists as a driver for policy' will be organised by the belgian presidency on 9 and 10 november in ostend, which is - as you may know - a belgian coastal city. the presidency invited the european parliament to attend on 15 july when it presented its priorities. the belgian presidency hopes that by organising this symposium it will contribute to the discussions currently under way to prepare the reform of the current common fisheries policy. a new common policy on this should be in place from 2013. scientists and the fishing industry often have different views and take different positions on fisheries and environmental management. the aim of the symposium is to discuss this issue in depth and to draw lessons from good practice in this area. to this end, it is envisaged to organise discussions around five themes: data collection and stock assessments, joint efforts to improve selectivity and reduce discards, communication between scientists and industry, improvement of the integrated consultation process and, finally, self-management. the results of the symposium will be used to initiate a debate at ministerial level at the agriculture and fisheries council in november. the council could then draw the appropriate conclusions.

question no 13 by jim higgins (h-0429/10):subject: trafficking in children: what measures will the council take to ensure that the member states fulfil their duty in combating the trafficking of children? in its latest report, the child protection organisation ecpat noted that ireland is one of the eu states with the worst record in the fight against the trafficking of children for sexual exploitation. although there are no reliable figures on child trafficking in ireland, this report has raised the alarm by stating that 441 children have disappeared while in the care of the irish state.
president of the council. − the legislation in force to prevent and combat trafficking in human beings is mainly the council framework decision of 19 july 2002 on combating trafficking in human beings, which obliges member states to make punishable offences related to trafficking in human beings, for the purpose of labour exploitation or sexual exploitation. a proposal for a directive to strengthen the fight against trafficking and the protection of victims, and a second proposal for a directive on the sexual exploitation and abuse of children and child pornography are currently being examined in the eu institutions. these proposals aim in particular at providing specific measures of assistance, assistance and protection for children who are victims of trafficking in human beings. they also contain provisions to improve the prosecution of offences committed outside the territory of the member states and rules to prevent such offences. on the basis of the stockholm programme, specific attention shall be given to children in particularly vulnerable situations, including children who are victims of sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as children who are victims of trafficking and unaccompanied minors. in the context of the union's immigration policy, it should also be added that the commission has adopted an action plan for unaccompanied minors, which proposes a common approach based on the principle of the best interests of the child, and identifies major areas of action such as prevention, reception and the search for sustainable solutions. following that action plan, the council, in its conclusions on unaccompanied minors adopted in june 2010, decided to request member states to strengthen measures concerning unaccompanied minors who are victims of trafficking in human beings by entrusting them to the competent authorities in the member state where they are located. as it is currently difficult to estimate the exact number of persons who are victims of trafficking in human beings within the union, or who are illegally brought into the union in the context of trafficking in human beings, and with a view to providing the european union with objective, reliable, comparable and up-to-date statistics, the council, in its conclusions of june 2009, adopted the establishment within the union of an informal network of national rapporteurs or equivalent mechanisms in the field of trafficking in human beings. this network, which should serve as a forum for the exchange of experience and best practice in the field of preventing and combating trafficking in human beings at european level, has been established. finally, a general guidance document on the fight against trafficking in human beings was adopted in november 2009. it is partly devoted to the question of child trafficking. as regards the part of the question which refers to a specific member state, it is not for the council to decide on individual cases.

question no 14 by liam aylward, on behalf of the ppe group: subject: european measures for job creation what measures are being taken at european level and in the member states to support and encourage efforts to create jobs? what are you doing to combat unemployment and what measures have been taken to ensure greater access to employment and the labour market throughout the eu, particularly in disadvantaged areas?
president of the council. - mr gallagher, thank you very much for allowing me to speak on this important matter. the member states are primarily responsible for defining and implementing their national employment policies. since the labour market situation differs from one member state to another, the measures to be taken will also necessarily vary, provided that they contribute, as a whole, to the achievement of the union's overall objectives. under the treaty on the functioning of the european union, these measures are coordinated within the european employment strategy, which includes employment guidelines and recommendations to member states. at its meeting in june 2010, the european council endorsed the general guidance on integrated guidelines for economic and employment policies, which is an essential tool for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy for jobs and growth. having taken into account the opinion of parliament adopted on 8 september 2010, the presidency will submit them to the council for adoption at its next epsco session on 21 october 2010. according to these guidelines, member states and the european union should implement reforms aimed at smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. reforms should aim to improve participation in the labour market, in particular for under-represented groups - young people, the elderly, the low-skilled, legal migrants - reduce structural unemployment and promote quality employment through measures affecting both labour supply and demand. they also aim to develop a skilled workforce to meet labour market needs, promote lifelong learning and stimulate entrepreneurship and small and medium-sized enterprises. the appropriate use of european funds, including the european social fund, will help to achieve these objectives and ensure better access to employment and the labour market throughout the european union, particularly in the less-favoured regions. in addition, through the joint annual employment report, the council, together with the commission, monitors the employment situation in the member states and in particular the implementation of the employment guidelines and recommendations. the latest joint employment report 2009-2010, which dates from spring 2010, gives a true picture of the type of measures taken by the different member states to improve the employment situation, and in particular that of young people and women. the council stressed, for example, that member states must also improve the business environment, stimulate job creation, including green jobs, and help companies to modernise their industrial base. given the importance of the european employment strategy for coordinating and improving the effectiveness of national employment policies, it will play a key role in the new governance context established by the european semester.
president of the council. - i refer you to the belgian presidency's programme on this subject, because it is true that the question was on employment and we concentrated in the reply on structural measures to promote employment, through the 2020 strategy and the guidelines. but it's true, you're absolutely right. we have in the belgian programme a whole series of measures which are aimed at reducing the administrative burden on small and mediumsized enterprises, on micro-enterprises which do not have the structural capacity to provide staff to analyse all the legislation in force, and in particular all that concerns aid to enterprises, which is sometimes far too complex for small enterprises. i know that in belgium, and in any case under the belgian presidency, the minister responsible for this matter intends, at an informal meeting he is organising, to emphasise these administrative hassles and administrative burdens which hamper the smooth running of small and mediumsized enterprises.

question no 17 by richard howitt, who has appointed kinga göncz as his alternate (h-0444/10):subject: progress on the eu horizontal anti-discrimination directive 2010 is the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion. as part of its programme, the belgian presidency expressed its desire to make progress in the fight against discrimination and for equality. in view of this commitment, could the council indicate what progress is being made towards agreement on the horizontal anti-discrimination directive, which the european parliament has already put to the vote at first reading? could the president-in-office of the council confirm that the definition of goods and services to be included in the directive will comply with the eu's obligation to implement the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities? could the council indicate what is the strategy to dispel the doubts and concerns that member states continue to raise on the issue of the economic cost of equality?
president of the council. - mr president, during the spanish presidency, the council continued its examination of the proposal for a directive and on 7 june 2010 it took note of a presidency report on the state of progress of the work. the report states that further in-depth examination of the proposal will be necessary, particularly as regards the scope, the disability provisions and the timetable for implementation. the members of the council also stressed the need to guarantee the greatest possible legal certainty and to ensure respect for the principle of subsidiarity. the proposal should be adopted in accordance with article 19 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which requires the unanimity of the members of the council. while the draft directive aims to achieve some of the objectives of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, this instrument is not intended to implement that convention legally, as it has a wider scope that goes beyond the competences of the european union. it goes without saying, however, that one of the objectives of the discussions currently taking place in the council is to ensure consistency with this convention. as regards the economic cost of equality, the discussion also focused on the concept of disproportionate burdens, which is precisely aimed at finding the right balance between the effective right to equal access and the economic cost of such access. if all efforts are made to reach unanimity, the council is not in a position to foresee the outcome of the negotiations or their duration.
president of the council. - mr president, i understand the subject and the natural impatience in this matter. the discussions have probably been going on for too long, but this is an innovative proposal with a very wide scope and enormous practical implications. i repeat, the unanimity of the member states and the consent of the european parliament are required for the directive to be adopted. complex negotiations are taking place within the council, which is devoting a great deal of energy to this issue. the working party on social affairs has already discussed this proposal on two occasions under the belgian presidency; i am sure that if this problem is not resolved during the belgian presidency, the next presidency, the hungarian one, will do everything possible to bring the debate to a conclusion.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission as a whole, as do i, believes that our objective is to develop a social market economy. i can say, for me personally and for my portfolio, that in this expression the ‘social’ is more important than the ‘market’. of course at the end of the day, the commission has to put forward, represent and implement a very balanced approach. however, i and vulnerable groups to be taken into account. in recent weeks i have made many speeches and i have called for caution in terms of the macroeconomic policies of member states. fiscal consolidation is inevitable because countries accumulated high debts. however, austerity – especially mindless austerity – and single-minded expenditure cuts are not inevitable. all member states, even those that are under pressure from the markets, have room to consider how to deliver a measured fiscal consolidation. everyone has the capacity to balance the various options, expenditure cuts or revenue increases; and they can apply fairness, they can take into account the interests of vulnerable groups. the commission has been calling for that. even in these difficult times, we are calling for social awareness. that is where the european year has been helping us a lot. this has been an awareness-raising campaign and to that extent it has been a success because it helped to deliver the two very important targets of europe 2020. without this campaign we would not have been successful in delivering the very ambitious targets on raising employment and reducing poverty in europe. of course nobody believes that this can be delivered overnight. we have to improve our instruments. i accept what the honourable member said about the european social fund (esf). it has not been functioning perfectly; but we are in the process of exploring where the esf should be improved in terms of innovation, what the esf should be dealing with, and how it should be used. this is all part of a process. there are series of conferences to discuss that, especially in the context of how to handle the situation of the roma population, among other issues. the belgian presidency is holding a conference specifically on how the esf could be more useful in reducing poverty. i would be doubtful about establishing a new fund. i think we first have to explore how the social fund could be used, with the available instruments, to improve social conditions. here, i would underline the role of the european investment bank in terms of developing the infrastructure and services in europe. nobody is calling for the privatisation of social services. these are predominantly member state competences. however, if the eu rules concerning public procurement or state aid, for example, are applied correctly, taking all important parameters into account, they will guarantee quality, cost effectiveness and transparency. these are very important objectives and we should not undermine these much in the focus of the commission’s work and very much in the focus of my personal agenda.

i am very pleased to see that the commission has taken the initiative to introduce a new system of penalties for infringements of the competition rules. it is a reaction to anti-competitive behaviour, a reaction which must be effective and forceful. a weak and insufficient reaction will be an incentive and a stimulus to infringement and therefore fines should be dissuasive; they should be dissuasive for the infringers but also have a general deterrent effect for all operators. it should be clear that unfair competition will not provide any advantage or benefit to those who do so. it is true that the commission has a wide margin of discretion in the application of fines. but discretion does not mean arbitrariness, because there are rules, there are limits, there are criteria, there is a procedure with guarantees and, in any case, there is judicial control. the treaty, regulation (ec) no 1/2003, the 2006 guidelines, the communication on the leniency programme also 2006, all constitute a framework that is working reasonably well. but the system can be improved. the experience gained from its application, the recommendations of experts and the legitimate concerns expressed by the institutions and some operators suggest that some issues should be addressed. transparency and predictability can be improved, and the impact on smes, employment and the sustainability of enterprises can be considered. the elements of flexibility on the amount and payments, as well as the link with leniency programmes and even how to overcome the divergences between the systems of the different member states should also be considered. the system can also be complemented by other appropriate instruments, such as focusing on individual liability, considering other remedies 'not only to put an end to anti-competitive behaviour but to prevent its recurrence', and launching private actions for damages, both individual and collective. all these issues must be tackled rigorously and in a systematic and positive manner, without casting doubt on the functioning of competition policy.

in writing. − the purpose of this text is to amend directive 2009/42/ec to make the collection of data by type of goods compulsory for maritime transport statistics. currently, 18 member states collect this data on a voluntary basis. five member states have no coastline and do not provide the data required by that directive. in most cases, the collection of the relevant data will not impose any additional burden on those providing it, as the member states concerned should be able to compile the data using existing sources of information (such as customs documents). the collection of data by type of goods is already mandatory for european statistics on road, rail and inland waterway transport. european statistics on all modes of transport must be compiled according to common concepts and standards, in order to achieve the fullest possible comparability between modes of transport, which is why i voted in favour of the text. the availability of complete and homogeneous statistics by type of goods for all modes of transport would provide a useful general framework for supporting and monitoring policy promoting commodity.
in writing. − the purpose of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and the council is to amend directive 2009/42/ec in order to make the collection of data by type of goods mandatory for maritime transport statistics. these data are currently collected on a voluntary basis by 18 member states. five member states have no maritime coast and do not provide any data under that directive. for the most part, the collection of the relevant data will not impose any additional burden on respondents as the member states concerned should be able to compile the data by using already existing data sources (for example, customs documents). the greens/efa have voted in favour of the proposal.
