in writing. - although i voted in favour of this proposal for aid, i consider that it is a measure to alleviate and mitigate the consequences of the capitalist model and does not represent any progress in the fight against the root causes of the crisis. i am in favour of the mobilisation of resources from the european globalisation adjustment fund for citizens made redundant as a result of structural changes in business models or as a direct consequence of the current economic and financial crisis. i believe that the more than two and a half million euros requested as assistance and supplementary aid for the more than 600 redundancies in the retail trade in the netherlands can be useful in the ultimate objective of facilitating the reintegration of these workers into employment. i also voted in favour, convinced that this assistance is complementary to the redundancy payments provided for in national legislation and collective agreements. the commission has also proposed that the egf should be used to finance the restructuring of the steel industry.
in writing. i supported the vote of the european parliament which approved, on tuesday 14 december 2010, the release of €35.6 million for france, whose atlantic coastline was partly devastated by the storm xynthia last february. this money will be used to finance the rehabilitation of infrastructure affected by the disaster. as a member of the european parliament representing the regions most affected, i welcome the release of these funds to repair the damage caused by the storm: it is a real relief for all the french departments affected. this mobilisation shows that for the european union solidarity is not a vain word. in conclusion, i would like to remind you that the storm xynthia in february 2010 affected a large part of france: the departments of charente-maritime and vendée were the most affected, causing 53 deaths and 80 injuries. the property damage was estimated at eur 1 425.43 million. in total, 35.6 million has been released from the eu solidarity fund to repair them.
in writing. − the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund in favour of portugal and france under point 26 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (iia). the iia allows the mobilisation of the solidarity fund within the annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. in 2010, so far, only one proposal to mobilise the solidarity fund has been submitted by the commission, a proposal of 24 september 2010 to mobilise eur 13.02 million following severe flooding in ireland in november 2009 (com(2010)0534). this proposal and the corresponding draft amending budget (dab no 8/2010) are still in the process of being adopted by the two arms of the budgetary authority. in parallel to the proposal to mobilise the solidarity fund in favour of portugal and france, the commission has presented a draft amending budget (dab no 9/2010 of 13 october 2010) in order to enter the corresponding commitment and payment appropriations in the 2010 budget as provided in point 26 of the iia.
in writing. − according to article 37(1) of the financial regulation, the commission may present draft amending budgets if there are ‘unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances’. on this aspect, and regarding the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund, the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund in favour of portugal and france on the basis of point 26 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (iia). the iia allows the mobilisation of the solidarity fund within the annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. the conditions for eligibility to the fund are detailed here and as well as in council regulation no 2012/2002 establishing the eusf. it is important to note that the objective of the fund is not to compensate private damage but to repair infrastructure and it is a tool for refinancing. in 2010, so far, only one proposal to mobilise the solidarity fund has been submitted by the commission, a proposal of 24 september 2010 to mobilise eur 13.02 million following severe flooding in ireland in november 2009 (com(2010)0534).
in writing. - i voted for aid to aragon. this autonomous community has a population density below the eu average (112 inhabitants per square km); its traditional economy is the cultivation of cereals and sheep farming; its retail trade has suffered 1 154 layoffs from 593 companies in a nine-month period; its unemployment in the service sector in february 2010 was 56%, with 73% of them women; 73.9% of the workers laid off were shop and market vendors; 14.4% were in unskilled jobs. it is regrettable that the measures were taken too late, 11 months after the first redundancies. it would be interesting to see what the outcome is of the temporary and extraordinary assistance measures for redundant workers which will be introduced for their reintegration into the labour market. but it should be clear that these actions should not replace those which companies are obliged to take on the basis of national legislation or collective agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the adaptation fund support to valencia because, as a consequence of the structural changes in world trade and the financial crisis, 544 redundancies in 143 companies have unexpectedly occurred between 13 april 2009 and 12 january 2010 in the valencia textile industry, redundancies which have had a great impact at local level. 61.7% of the redundant are men and 22% are over 55 years old; 79.9% of them have only basic education and 4 of them are disabled. i believe that the training they will receive during the 14 months of parttime paid work experience will improve their professional qualifications so that they can enter the labour market. as in the previous case, it is regrettable that the measures were applied late, one year and two months after the first redundancies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this initiative so that 330 of the 528 people who were made redundant in the last nine months in 66 companies in valencia in the natural stone processing sector can receive additional support to make it possible for them to re-enter the labour market. of these, 62% are over 45 years old, three have a disability, 51% have no formal education and 34.4% have only basic education. this community has received other aid for job losses in the manufacturing sector. it must therefore take other measures as a matter of urgency. the mobilisation of the egf can only be a part of these measures. and finally, i must regret once again that the measures taken by the spanish state have been implemented so late: one year and three months after the dismissals, when such measures must be implemented immediately and urgently.
in writing. - the crisis has led to a 28% drop in vehicle registrations. in terres de l'ebre (catalonia), employment in the service sector is 60%. the closure of lear automotive has caused a 4% increase in the unemployment rate in this region, which in 2009 stood at 22.7%. the aid is intended to provide a package of personalised services similar to other aid granted in the same region, and to the same sector, in another case covering 1 429 of the 2 330 redundancies. this dossier will apply to 508 of the 515 redundancies recorded in a four-month period in 2010 due to the closure of the lear automotive company. i voted in favour of this initiative so that its implementation will allow the people concerned to return to the world of work and help to reduce unemployment.
in writing. − with the adoption of this text, the ep has requested the institutions involved to make the necessary efforts to accelerate the mobilisation of the egf. it also recalls the institutions’ commitment to ensuring a smooth and rapid procedure for the adoption of decisions on the mobilisation of the egf, providing one-off, time-limited individual support geared to helping workers who have suffered redundancies as a result of globalisation and the financial and economic crisis. it emphasises the role that the egf can play in the reintegration of workers made redundant into the labour market. finally, it stresses that, in accordance with article 6 of the egf regulation, it should be ensured that the egf supports the reintegration of individual redundant workers into employment, and reiterates that assistance from the egf must not replace actions which are the responsibility of companies by virtue of national law or collective agreements, nor measures restructuring companies or sectors.
in writing. − in 2001, the commission presented a proposal for a directive concerning the status of third-country nationals who are long-term residents. in this proposal, it was originally foreseen that refugees could qualify for long-term resident status after five years of legal and continuous residence in a member state. in the course of the negotiations, it was nevertheless decided by the member states to exclude refugees from the scope of the directive. subsequently, in the joint statement from the council and the commission, made at the jha council of 8 may 2003, it was agreed that the commission would table a proposal for a directive on the extension of long-term resident status to refugees and persons under subsidiary protection. this proposal was tabled by the commission in june 2007 using the same legal base as the act it was supposed to amend, i.e. articles 63(3)(a) and 63(4) of the ec treaty. the main objective of the proposal was to give beneficiaries of international protection who have been legally residing in a member state for a period of 5 years legal certainty about their right of residence in a member state, as well as a set of rights comparable to those of eu nationals.
in writing. − the enlargement of the european union to 25 member states in 2004 and then to 27 in 2007 was an opportunity for the union to create a new framework for cooperation with its neighbours to the east and the south. the european union thus engaged in an enlarged neighbourhood policy extending as far as the countries of the south caucasus region and aimed at deepening its relations with the countries located at the eu's external borders, promoting their security, stability and development and preventing new divisions on the european continent. europe thus signalled its growing interest in the states of the south caucasus and it must today pursue its engagement with the countries of this region as an area to be protected near its new frontiers. the process of deepening relations between the eu and the countries of the south caucasus, including georgia, will undoubtedly also help to improve the exercise of justice and respect for freedom. the two agreements recently concluded with georgia – one on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation and the other on facilitation of the issuance of visas – will contribute fully to achieving these objectives.
in writing. − the multiplication of major disasters (natural/man made) outside the european union in recent years has led to increased calls to improve the effectiveness of the existing eu disaster-response capacity. if the eu disaster-response capacity has constantly evolved since the establishment of the community civil protection mechanism in 2001, the rapporteur believes that much more needs to be done to ensure a coordinated, coherent and visible eu response. this need for a more coherent response was also highlighted in the latest communication from the commission on ‘reinforcing the union’s disaster response capacity’, which dates back to march 2008. this communication was supposed to be a first step on the road to a comprehensive and integrated eu response. it included an action plan with a number of practical actions to gradually build up more integrated coordination between the various instruments for disaster response. today we have parliament’s response to that problem.
in writing. − it seems that a significant consequence of the competition brought about by the implementation of mifid has been market fragmentation which has in itself encouraged the explosive growth of hft strategies. regulation needs to recognise that these technological advances are in need of suitable provisions in the legislation so that they do not fall through regulatory gaps and inadvertently cause systemic risk to the overall functioning of the markets. that is, in summary, the proposal in the text adopted today by the ep.
in writing. − chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (cbrn) risks present a new dimension of possible terrorist attacks, accidents, natural disasters and/or pandemics due to their transnational character and mass-scale victimisation. an appropriate response against such a danger does not include only ex-post-facto intervention programmes but starts much earlier when dealing with such materials, their proper storage, limited access, controls, etc. at the same time, an aftermath intervention demands large-scale cooperation between different national authorities inside a member state (civil protection, military, law enforcement, etc.) as well as between national authorities of different member states and eu bodies. therefore, an all-hazard coordinated approach is needed. that is what we intend to do with the adoption of this report.
in writing. − over the last few decades, the decentralisation of powers in several member states has considerably reinforced regional and local authorities’ competences in the delivery of community policies. the incorporation by the reform treaty of sub-national subsidiarity into community law for policies of shared competence today allows territorial authorities to be more deeply involved in the decision-making process, both for the design and the implementation of policies, as fully dignified partners to participate in achieving the community objectives. this important step towards better multi-level governance answers repeated requests by parliament to reinforce the involvement of the sub-national authorities in the conception of policies always respecting the different national constitutional assets.
in writing. − when the regulation now being amended was adopted on 19 february 2004, frontex was yet to be officially established. it was eight months later, on 26 october 2004, that the council adopted the regulation establishing a european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders. by virtue of the remits set out in its rules of procedure, frontex is responsible for carrying out risk analysis based on the information gathered by the competent authorities in the member states, for facilitating operational cooperation between the member states and third countries, and for cooperating with the competent authorities of third countries and with international organisations through, for example, exchanges of experience on border control issues, the training of border guards, operational information exchanges and joint operations. the amendments proposed here are appropriate and necessary. the troubled times that the european union is experiencing demand appropriate management of immigration flows. this should be seen as having two facets: management of legal immigration and management of illegal and clandestine immigration.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has rejected this single permit proposal. today's vote opens new negotiations and gives a negative answer to the allocation of rights according to the market value of workers. this directive, far from guaranteeing a common set of rights for all migrant workers, based on equal treatment and non-discrimination, proposed a fragmented view of legal migration, where the market value of a migrant worker would determine the extent of his rights! on the eve of the 20th anniversary of the un convention on the protection of the rights of migrant workers and members of their families, this hierarchy is totally unacceptable: the union must finally incorporate the conclusions of numerous studies which demonstrate that the individual as well as collective, economic and societal benefits, for host societies as well as those of origin, go hand in hand with the full and effective exercise by migrants of their rights. the greens will continue to exercise the utmost vigilance to help equip the union with an ambitious migration policy based on the principle of the universality and indivisibility of fundamental rights. that will be the issue in the new discussions opened up by the rejection of this bad agreement.
in writing. − the proposal for a directive on the european protection order, submitted by 12 member states, is an initiative aimed at preventing crime. even when member states have provided for protection orders for victims, the resulting enforcement measures stop at the border of the issuing state. victims, however, may move from one member state to another for many reasons, not least to escape crime. because they move in this way they are defenceless when judicial and law enforcement cooperation fails to protect them by implementing a rapid, effective, europe-wide early-warning and prevention mechanism. setting up a cooperation arrangement along these lines is the aim behind this initiative. the action taken by member states shows that crime can be prevented at european level when the aggressor or aggressors are identified.
in writing. − this legislation represents an important step forward in combating this inhumane and degrading crime, and we welcome its adoption today. however, the aim of the directive was to address prevention, prosecution and protection, and the greens regret that the provisions on victim protection are not as strong as we believe is possible and necessary. the position of victims and their legal status or their rights to legal assistance could and should have been much stronger. hopefully, the commission will now come forward with a proposal to revise the directive on residence permits for victims of trafficking so that we get a truly holistic approach to tackling this hideous crime, as envisaged from the beginning. i am also glad that there is no direct reference requiring member states to take legal measures to penalise those who use services (for example, dining in a restaurant in which victims of trafficking are working). besides the intricacy and legal uncertainty of differentiating the 'what, who and when' in all of this, such measures actually risk bringing victims of trafficking further outside the reach of the authorities.
in writing. − we voted against this agreement because: it aims to return people to a country where, according to the unhcr global appeal 2010–2011, around 212 000 people were internally displaced for more than 16 years, living in need of shelter and means to become self-sufficient, where sexual and gender-based violence is rife in all parts of society and police ill-treatment is tolerated; it also applies to those former residents of abkhazia and south ossetia who do not have any de facto links to georgia; it does not include strict safeguards concerning the violation of fundamental rights and guaranteeing high standards of reception, which are poor in georgia; it contains numerous loopholes and ambiguities which might be clarified in the joint readmission committee in which parliament regrettably has no say, which would be entirely legitimate regarding its new competences; it does not guarantee adequately the protection of personal data – data can be forwarded to ‘other bodies’ without requiring the consent of the person involved.
in writing. - in the course of drawing up this report our group has often expressed substantive disagreements with the line suggested by the author, so that in the end we had no choice but to vote against it.

the following is the report by mr jean-paul gauzès, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies (com (2010) 0289 - c7-0143/2010 - 2010/0160 (cod)) (a7-0340/2010).
mr president, president-in-office of the council, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating the commissioner and the parliamentary delegation, led by our colleague mr leinen, on the work they have done in cancun, a meeting which i was unfortunately unable to attend. i believe that cancun and its results can be seen, in the same way as my colleague mr seeber said, from the angle of copenhagen: cancun seen from copenhagen. and cancun seen from copenhagen has a first conclusion, and that is that between the two summits there was a fundamental differential factor. in copenhagen expectations were very high and in cancun expectations were much more realistic, as a result of which the assessment of copenhagen was very negative and, on the other hand, that of cancun, both by those who have participated and by the media in general, has been very positive. cancun has learned from copenhagen, and i think this is a very interesting first conclusion. i think that measures have been taken and agreements reached which are certainly not really groundbreaking, but which can be very interesting from the point of view of efficiency. among other things, the creation of a committee and a technology network to promote technological cooperation seems to me extremely important - we are going to vote on a report at this part-session on energy efficiency, which is one of the key elements for an effective fight against climate change - and then issues such as the world bank becoming more involved or the official recognition of countries' actions in relation to emission reductions returning to the united nations procedure and framework also seem very positive to me. finally, i would like to say that it is a year's journey to south africa. it would be very interesting if, just as cancun has learned from copenhagen, we now learn from kyoto and achieve an international framework of reference for an agreement on the fight against climate change that is more flexible, more transparent, more effective and more inclusive.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, the directive adopted in 2009 was a success because it updates the regulatory framework that has been governing the safety of toys. it is a big step in the right direction because it shows us the way forward, but it is not enough. we must always be vigilant and watchful that the toys on the market do not endanger the safety and health of children. all toys on the market must comply with the legislation in force. we need to review and improve the monitoring mechanisms for detecting dangerous toys, whether for substances considered toxic - cmr substances - or for fragrances or other dangerous substances, such as hpa compounds. there is a need for clearer rules on the warning regarding the minimum age and the dangers of inappropriate use. we must ensure that the recommended age for toys is based on studies of children's behaviour. we must be able to adapt our legislation to scientific progress, supported by sound studies, and be more rigorous in the surveillance of the market and the importation of toys. it is necessary to work together and to strengthen cooperation between member states and to have customs working together to control the route of imported toys. the citizens are preparing to go christmas shopping and we must ensure that the products they buy meet all the safety requirements.
madam president, what we need at the moment are clear rules, and what we are doing is the exact opposite. i shall therefore make some proposals to restore clarity. this parliament wants the european semester to concentrate on a number of discussions which are now scattered and do not reach public opinion. we want the political responses to the recommendations that are addressed to the member states during this semester to be taken into account when setting the sanctions provided for in the legislative package on governance. in the legislative package, my group wants to make it clear that there are no magic recipes for getting out of the crisis. there are the known recipes for budgetary discipline and structural reforms to maintain competitiveness. with regard to the crisis mechanism - i mentioned it to you yesterday, commissioner - president barroso promised us here that it would be a european mechanism. the council is proposing an intergovernmental mechanism today. is that european in mr barroso's terminology because the fund will apparently be in europe and not in the cayman islands, or does the commission want to help us to make a mechanism based on the community method in which this parliament has a say? and in the case of eurobonds, the commission, the oecd, the experts say it is a good idea, but they say it is a premature idea, and that is why we are late. what i am proposing to the commission is that we start a debate on saving a eurobond system which gives reasonable financing to virtuous countries and punishes the non-virtuous by going to the markets at genuinely dissuasive rates. that is the only way to properly combine fiscal discipline and economic growth. and don't come at me with that if it's early or it's late, because now, what we know, is that we've always been late. let's see if, for once, changing the rules, we get there early.
madam president, this year that is ending - 2010 - has been described more than once as a year in which we have lived dangerously. that is why i think the debate should be useful to highlight the lessons of 2010 so that we can draw conclusions in 2011. the first concerns the unsustainable asymmetries between the financial components of the european economy and the imbalances in its real economy. secondly, the unsustainable asymmetry between the single currency and the requirements of coordination of economic, fiscal and budgetary policies, with a still fragile balance sheet. the third and most important point concerns the asymmetry between the intensity of the crisis and the slowness of the response times. from an economic point of view, this means that the european central bank must be more active in the fight against the speculative assault on sovereign debt and we must lay the foundations in 2011 for a european debt agency capable of issuing eurobonds. the commission has also been asked to present a report on the implementation of the stability and growth pact, which is a report on the need for taxation, the financial levy and the levy against speculation, short-term speculative transactions and the need for own resources in the european union. but one debate that matters to this parliament is the debate on the political consequences of the crisis, because the motto of the european union - i stress this again - is 'united in diversity', in no case 'united in the face of adversity'. this parliament must therefore stand up to those who wish to stigmatise some member states against others, dividing european public opinion, europeans against europeans. this parliament represents 500 million europeans in a union of 27 states, none of which, like the orwell farm, is more equal than the other.
on behalf of the ppe group madam president, the group of the european people's party will vote enthusiastically on this report and i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs, the commission and the council on this agreement. we coined the term 'democratic deficit' in the 1980s. we are not talking about the european parliament, but about the council of ministers, which is the body that makes decisions in the european union, on the basis of proposals from the commission, and this parliament is only consulted. the battle of this parliament since the 1980s, through the maastricht, amsterdam, nice, constitutional and lisbon treaties, has been to close this democratic gap, and i believe that with the lisbon treaty, with the new powers of the european parliament, with the participation of the national parliaments, we have achieved that objective. and we are rounding it off today with this citizens' legislative initiative, which was due, in the work of the convention, to the good cooperation between the national parliaments and the european parliament. i would like to mention the names of our german social democrat colleague, jürgen meyer, and alain lamassoure, who brought this initiative to the plenary of the convention and who made it happen. so i think we have come full circle, madam president. i believe that when we vote on the initiative today, we will have put on the table the death certificate of the concept of 'democratic deficit'. and now, ladies and gentlemen, we must act responsibly, and today we have the opportunity to do so. by voting on the union's budget, we will be doing what is expected of us: a responsible parliament and a co-decision parliament. i think it is a good day for europe, ladies and gentlemen.
the s&d group is calling for a new approach to the problem of the unfinished business of democracy, which is a new approach to the problem of the unfinished business of democracy. and indeed, we are in the middle of an unfinished journey in which many stages have been covered, but we are in a period of risk, of uncertainty and of many doubts. but within these doubts, we have certainties. the first is that the building that has stood the test has been that of representative democracy: it is the building of our institutions; without free parliaments based on the will of the people, democracy has never survived. but it is also true that democracy today needs innovations, reforms, changes that improve the quality, maintaining the buildings that have served us so far and maintaining the strength of its foundations. what kind of changes do we need? we need to move towards a democracy that broadens the participatory forum; that citizens are more than voters every four or five years; a democracy that broadens the deliberative space, where citizens discuss, reason, exchange their opinions; and a democracy that broadens social capital, where citizens break out of their isolation and become part of the community. and we also need a european dimension to that democracy. i think that is what we have achieved with the regulation of this citizens' initiative. from now on there are no longer two legitimations, there are two voices of the citizens: one is in this parliament and the other is in the citizens' initiative. and with that, we will make a stronger, more participatory and more legitimate democracy.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the purpose of the regulation is to create legal certainty for couples wishing to separate or divorce when they belong to different states of the union, by guaranteeing predictability and flexibility. the initiative adopted has been a step forward in this respect, but it is regrettable, first of all, that the opportunity to extend the scope of application to the recognition of marriages, nullity, guardianship of children and inheritances has been lost. nor is there any mention of the existence of other types of unions, such as those between homosexual couples, which are recognised in some member states. secondly, it is also regrettable that only 15 of the 27 member states are prepared to sign up to this enhanced cooperation, which will be detrimental to the citizens of the countries that do not. i therefore hope and hope that in the future the scope and the number of countries which are in favour of this enhanced cooperation will be extended, because they owe it to the citizens they represent.
in writing. − this text sets out to solve problems such as the following. a and b are nationals of different member states who entered into a same-sex marriage in one of the member states which have introduced legislation to permit such marriages. they have been habitually resident for three years in a member state which does not permit same-sex marriages but participated in the adoption of the regulation on applicable law under the enhanced cooperation procedure. a and b wish to dissolve their marriage. under the rules of regulation no 2201/2003 on jurisdiction, the only courts having jurisdiction in those circumstances are the courts of the member state in which they are habitually resident. this is patently not fair on the couple concerned, who would be put to a considerable amount of inconvenience and loss of time in order to bring their divorce proceedings within the jurisdiction of another court.
in writing. - i could not support this report because, although i support many of the points in it and the general proposal to strengthen transparency and improve the information and supervision of credit agencies and other financial institutions, this proposal will serve the interests of investors, professionals far removed from what has been called the 'real economy', as it gives them greater legal certainty. so while i believe that, as this proposal suggests, we must work hard for transparency and the right to clear information in the financial system, i believe that it is more necessary to put an end to financial speculation and to make a regulatory effort to put financial markets under the protection of the states. this report works along the lines of transparency, information and a certain degree of supervision of financial operators, but it does so in a timid way and from a complacent approach to the financial and pro-capitalist industry, which i neither share nor support.
in writing. − the global financial crisis, to which the credit rating agencies made their contribution, showed the need to set up a mechanism for monitoring and supervising these agencies. this was the purpose behind the adoption, in 2009, of regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies. this made it possible to establish a european system for registering and supervising credit rating agencies which issue ratings used in the european union. it also lays down the conditions for the use in the european union of ratings issued by third-country agencies, by applying a double system of equivalence and endorsement of ratings. during the debates preceding the adoption of regulation (ec) no 1060/2009, your rapporteur stressed the need for eu-wide joint oversight of credit rating agencies’ products and integrated supervision of them. this principle was upheld and the commission undertook to draft a legislative proposal along these lines. the agreement reached on the architecture of european supervision which will enter into force on 1 january 2011 now makes the effective implementation of rating agency supervision possible. it is stressed in the regulation establishing the esma that this authority will exercise its own supervisory powers in relation, in particular, to credit rating agencies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive repealing eight council directives on metrology because, like the rapporteur, i support the overall objective of better regulation. i also support the view that 'more time should be given to member states to examine whether the repeal of directives will not lead to legal uncertainty'. i believe that it is necessary to repeal and simplify these directives which refer to measuring instruments by revising the legal instrument which is the basis of metrology: the directive on measuring instruments. in general, i consider the simplification of the eu legislative acquis to be a positive development, as it can improve citizens' access to the eu's legislative work and make it possible to work more efficiently in this area.
in writing. − with this vote, the ep shows that it favours the general objective of better regulation. however, with regard to this proposal it is not that clear what the best option will be. the commission concludes in their impact assessment, when looking at the different options concerning these 8 metrology directives (full repeal, repeal with conditions, do nothing), that ‘no option stands out’. still, for reasons of better regulation, the commission favours the full repeal of all directives (and relies on mutual recognition of national regulation) above harmonisation (i.e. re-regulation in mid). the ep is of the opinion that member states should be given more time to investigate whether repealing the directives will lead to legal uncertainty which makes european harmonisation of rules necessary. therefore we have opted for a solution where the directives will be repealed and which also provides sufficient time to analyse the possible consequences in context with the broader review of the basic legal instrument in this field, the ‘measurement instruments directive’ (2004/22/ec).

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the effects of advertising on consumer behaviour as it clearly aims at improving the existing legislative framework for consumer protection against advertising and the necessary revision of it in the light of new forms of advertising which are not regulated. i also gave my support to the report as it seeks to improve harmonisation between member states to avoid legal loopholes which allow companies to implement misleading advertising practices in the eu member states. i think it is appropriate to refer to the mechanisms of covert advertising that have developed and take place on the internet, where, in many cases, advertising is disguised by opinions or comments on social networks, forums or blogs. i also welcome the concern that this report conveys to the council and the commission about the real risk posed by companies that are both content providers and advertising concessionaires. these are the main reasons, among others, why i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this report deals with unfair commercial practices in the advertising field, as defined in the unfair commercial practices directive (ucpd), and concentrates on issues arising from the development of new advertising practices and technologies. it does not discuss b2b relations, which are covered inter alia by directive 2006/114/ec. advertising is a tool that benefits both the internal market (oiling the wheels of economic activity by stimulating competition, competitiveness, innovation and creativity) and consumers (by increasing choice and lowering prices). it is a key economic sector: the eu online advertising market alone is worth more than eur 14 billion. however, it must not be idealised: advertising can also involve unfair practices, intrude into public spaces (e.g. in the form of advertising billboards) and the private arena (e.g. in the form of unsolicited e-mails), target vulnerable groups of people (such as children and those in excessive debt), create potential entry barriers to the internal market (where the outlay required is too high) and distort the internal market (by causing consumers to buy goods or services they would not normally have purchased).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the mandatory 20% energy efficiency target is important not only in terms of co2 reduction, which it is, but also in social terms. a large part of european household expenditure is spent on energy bills. introducing efficiency measures that reduce energy expenditure and contribute to reducing energy poverty is a socialist objective.
in writing. − this report is a powerful and timely reminder to the commission and the council of the importance of a binding energy-saving target ahead of the crucial energy summit on 4 february 2011 and as the commission prepares its energy efficiency action plan. ambitious eu measures on energy saving and efficiency are essential if europe is to respond to the challenges of energy security and climate change. they also make economic sense, create jobs and save consumers money on their energy bills. until now, member states have been reneging on their pledge to reduce energy consumption by 20% by 2020, by making insufficient progress. making the target binding will help (as in the case of renewable energy) to ensure that the eu governments actually deliver on this potential. the report also calls for stronger measures to address the energy consumption of buildings, notably by renovating the existing building stock. with buildings accounting for 40% of energy consumption in the eu, it is essential to tackle this sector head on. the greens hope that the eu energy summit will also address this crucial issue.
president of the council. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am delighted that the public is here. that's good! i am of course grateful to parliament for putting this matter on the agenda for this plenary. it allows us to address an important subject which has been the subject of considerable work in the council in recent months. i am, of course, aware of the importance which this parliament attaches to economic governance and its links with broader social issues, as set out in article 9 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the obligation under article 9 applies to the definition and implementation of all union policies and actions, including therefore all work on future economic governance. i would first like to recall that during the belgian presidency the importance of implementing article 9 and therefore the cross-cutting clause was mentioned on several occasions. i would like to recall the conclusions adopted by the council on 6 december on the social dimension in the context of an integrated europe 2020 strategy. these conclusions call on the european commission to strengthen and encourage the use of the existing social impact assessment system. it asked the commission to draw up a report on the way article 9 is implemented in european work and policies through the open method of coordination. it also called on the commission to look into ways of implementing social mainstreaming and therefore article 9 in the context of its flagship initiative, the european platform against poverty, which is due to be published in the very next few days. with regard to the new macroeconomic surveillance and coordination mechanism, the council sees employment and social protection not only as outcomes that could be affected by the new macroeconomic surveillance framework and whose impact should be studied, but also as factors for macroeconomic and budgetary growth in the short and medium term. this is an important element if we are to avoid an unbalanced macroeconomic framework and preserve the institutional balance required by the treaties. the council's desire to give concrete prominence to article 9 is also evident in the context of the european semester, which must reflect, in an integrated vision, a balanced position between the europe 2020 strategy and the stability pact. the principles contained in article 9 must therefore be transposed across all these documents and legislative measures to form an integrated whole. the council worked in two phases to this end. the first phase of the council's work was to articulate the european employment strategy provided for in the treaty and the new economic governance framework. in the conclusions adopted on 21 october, the council defined the place of the european employment strategy in economic governance. in the second phase, at the council meeting on 6 december, the council adopted a new instrument for multilateral monitoring of employment and social policies (joint assessment framework) which will allow better monitoring of the employment and social integration policies of the member states and, therefore, better account to be taken of these dimensions at european level. these new instruments will have to be mobilised in the preventive phase of macroeconomic surveillance in order to pay sufficient attention to labour market situations and social problems which could weaken emu. they will of course also be central instruments for the thematic monitoring of the europe 2020 strategy. the council also recalled its intention to contribute to both thematic surveillance based on the five broad objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and macroeconomic surveillance, as these two surveillance frameworks are closely linked. and, following the request of the belgian presidency, the social protection committee delivered an opinion on the social dimension of the europe 2020 strategy, in which it stressed the synergy between the priorities of the 2020 strategy and the inseparable whole of the objectives set by the european council. i would also point out that the council has mentioned article 9 in other conclusions: the conclusions on pensions and the council conclusions on social services of general interest. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, our discussion this afternoon allows us to address a number of issues relating to economic governance and, in particular, its social aspects. as president of the council, i am of course listening to your speeches and i look forward to a fruitful exchange of views which will help us all in the subsequent negotiations.
member of the commission. − madam president, article 9 of the lisbon treaty, to which you are referring, really defines the specific features of the european social economic model. when you read our europe 2020 strategy you can see it explicit reinforces this very model of europe by bringing together efforts to improve performance in areas such as labour participation, lifelong education, labour adaptability and mobility and social inclusion. however, this is not a sufficient answer at this time of severe challenges, when the climate of crisis in europe is affecting negatively, or even dramatically, the real economy, public finances, the labour market and the quality of life in europe. to address the challenges revealed by the crisis, the commission has launched several policy initiatives. to reinforce the stability of our financial system, the eu has agreed on a new architecture for financial regulation. this has been debated in parliament. secondly, to address the challenges to public finances and macroeconomic imbalances, the european commission has proposed a comprehensive strengthening of economic governance in the european union, the legislative package you referred to in your question. the package includes, as you know, proposals to address excessive public debt more seriously than in the past by defining a satisfactory pace of debt reduction. it also proposes minimum requirements for national fiscal frameworks to ensure that they are in line with treaty obligations as well as a monitoring system for macroeconomic imbalances such as large current account deficits or bubbles in the housing market. it underlines prevention and prudence to ensure better preparedness in times of economic downturn. to ensure the credibility of the new framework, the commission is proposing a wide range of sanctions that should start kicking in at an early stage. the philosophy behind the proposed legislation is that it should help member states to follow disciplined policies and lay the basis for stable long-term growth performance, which is critical to the welfare of european citizens, while making an important contribution to the prevention of future crises. given the current economic situation it is really important to have this economic governance framework in place as soon as possible. as to the impact assessment, the government reforms were prepared by far-reaching analysis in the emu@10 study in 2008. also, in preparing and following up the commission communications announcing the new governance structures of the so-called eu semester that were adopted in may and june 2010, the commission discussed its proposal with many stakeholders alongside the european parliament and the council and promoted vigorous, broad-based debate of the issues. and of course, we was developed the proposals in the light of past performance and lessons learnt. and what are the major lessons? the major lesson is that preventive action is much more valuable than imposing corrective sanctions on a state that is already in difficulties. therefore our emphasis is on influencing positively the national policy mix responsible – and here is the real responsibility – for the trade-off between real economic revival and growth, and austerity and consolidation of public finances. europe needs both.
on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, mr president, commissioner, following on from mrs berès's question, i would like to stress the economic model on which we in the european people's party are based: the social market economy, which means that we must put all our energies into action to get out of the crisis, to fight poverty but, much more than that, to ensure the social inclusion of a number of our fellow european citizens who are now on the verge of the crisis. we must now be concerned with this social inclusion, on the one hand to ensure that these citizens return to work, which is the development of employment in the fight against the crisis, but on the other hand, and this is extremely important, that in the coming years we can have, in all the member states, training plans, initial training measures and continuing training measures, which enable our fellow european citizens to adapt to the jobs of tomorrow, to the new skills we will need, to the raising of the level of skills expected in the 2020 strategy. so, based on this article 9, we see clearly that there is an impact to be developed also, extremely important, beyond everything that is done in terms of financial systems, so that we can have educated citizens who can be totally stakeholders totally in society, because they are active in this society, and active means trained, ready to hold the jobs of tomorrow. i therefore ask the commission's policies to be consistent with this objective, otherwise we will miss the objective of a europe with strong social cohesion.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the eyes of the citizens are on the european union; they know that the process of european integration has placed many aspects of their lives under the responsibility of the community institutions: many decisions are taken in the common area. many of the traditional instruments of the states have also been transferred to the european level and economic policies are a matter of common concern at european level - this is recognised by everyone - and the european union is therefore at the centre of this crisis: that is where the eyes are. we are not - as some claim - in a 'post-crisis' scenario, at most, we may be in a 'post-recession' scenario. the growth forecast for this year will be low and uneven and the problem is that next year, the forecasts indicate that it could still fall slightly. the number of unemployed in the european union now stands at 23 million. it is a crisis which has opened up a major social gap and which has also put pressure on public finances, even calling into question the future of the euro. strengthening the economic governance of the european union is essential to respond to the crisis and secure the future of the community project. it is necessary to meet our common challenges of restoring growth and jobs, changing the economic model and driving global sustainable development, and we must do so by securing the future of the european social model. the first economic crisis, the crisis of 1929, taught us that the public authorities were committed to restoring growth and employment; the second, the reconstruction of europe after the second world war, taught us that the building of the new europe had to be based on social justice. none of these lessons should be forgotten and both should be fully interwoven in the future of a sustainable europe. our treaty on the functioning of the eu, in article 9, says that 'in defining and implementing its policies and actions, the union shall take into account requirements relating to the promotion of a high level of employment, the guarantee of adequate social protection, the fight against social exclusion and a high level of education, training and protection of human health'. so it's not just about austerity. austerity can lead to contraction. we need policies which are also pro-growth, and therefore responsible policies. nor is it about growing first and then sharing: we have learned that sharing contributes to growth. nor is progress to be made in order to meet the basic needs of citizens: we have learned that education, health, social security and public services are fundamental to the progress of societies. if they do not exist, they are costs that weigh on the future of our society, and a healthy economy is not possible in a sick society. that is why we are asking the following questions: should the future legislative framework on economic governance be in line with the model of social europe, with article 9 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union? is there really an impact assessment? and do we really want president barroso to deliver on his commitment to social impact and to state clearly that europe needs a new social pact, also in taxation standards, in labour standards, a model that ensures employment, equity, environmental responsibility and global development? any other reform will be insufficient.
madam president, the new strategic concept of nato, born in lisbon, has been established to try to meet and adapt, firstly, to a new context, namely the disappearance of the bloc system and the end of the cold war and, secondly, to adapt to the new configuration of threats, especially to globalisation and to the fact that our armies have no apparent enemies and that our enemies have no armies. on the basis of this new strategic approach and always taking into account article 5 of the washington treaty as regards mutual assistance, there are three aspects which interest me. firstly, how to shape this strategic alliance with europe: i would like to ask you, mrs ashton, whether you think that turkey should participate as much as possible in the actions and development of the common foreign and security policy. secondly, the ratification of the start treaty by the new united states congress. do you think that this new strategic approach will be affected if this ratification does not take place? and finally, what is your view, mrs ashton, on the question of the missile shield? do you think this notion compromises the thesis of reducing nuclear arsenals in any way? because it seems that there are conflicting views among the member states.
madam president, mrs ashton, you know perfectly well that my group in this parliament is opposed to the existence of nato. it is totally opposed, among other things, because we are not in favour of any state in the world - or group of states, such as the nato military alliance - being able to use force without the express mandate of the united nations security council. since 1999, at its washington summit, nato has endorsed the possibility of using force without a mandate from the security council in this strategic concept. it is a step backwards and a frontal attack on the international law which was so hard to build up after the two world wars. we therefore do not share that philosophy, we do not share it with nato or any state which would presume to use force without such an express mandate. and, furthermore, it goes right into what were civil responses to problems that generate insecurity: organized crime, terrorism... it has never been a matter of military response, always civilian, of international police space, of judicial space and therefore we do not consider it to require a military response, nor the risk associated with natural resources or uncontrolled mass migration movements. they're not a matter of military response. the greatest killers in the world are hunger and poverty - the main weapons of mass destruction - and that cannot be opposed by a military force of the characteristics of nato.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the lisbon summit has certainly served to modernise nato and to adapt it to the new security challenges. we should welcome the fact that the new strategic concept adds new challenges, such as terrorism, the fight against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, cyber defence and energy security. it is also welcome that the new concept points to the need to strengthen the strategic relationship between nato and the european union. however, a clear division of labour is still lacking, so as to be efficient and not to redouble efforts in times of crisis. the treaty of lisbon has brought about a breakthrough in the common security and defence policy, which we must now consolidate. the objective is clear: the european union must be able to mobilise the civilian and military capabilities needed to assume its international responsibilities, and the common security and defence policy must make an important contribution to atlantic security. but what is not clear is how this collaboration with the alliance will be organised to make it really effective. it would be important, mrs ashton, if you could tell us more about this.
the following is the report by józsef szájer , on behalf of the committee on legal affairs , on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers (com (2010) 0083 - c7-0073/2010 - 2010/0051 (cod)) (a7-0355/2010).
the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy has adopted a number of amendments. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the treaty of lisbon introduces substantial changes in the process of developing and implementing community legislation, by distinguishing between delegated and implementing acts. the earlier original legislation provided only for enforcement measures. this regulation is essential for an orderly transition from the old to the new system and for the proper exercise of the implementing powers conferred on the commission in accordance with the new treaty of lisbon. it strengthens the democratic principle by recognising the right of parliament to scrutinise, increases transparency with the annual report and incorporates a revision clause to improve it in the light of experience. it therefore meets the requirements of the committee on economic and monetary affairs. in the area of financial services, it will contribute to increasing legal certainty and the effectiveness of legislation. it complements the objective of the omnibus directive to limit the powers conferred on the commission under the old framework to a period of three years from the entry into force of the new treaty, and provides for the adoption of the implementing technical standards, which are envisaged in the new supervisory architecture and sectoral regulation in the field of financial services. i am therefore, as rapporteur for the committee on economic and monetary affairs, very pleased and i congratulate mr szájer. i thank the president for his generosity and i also wish you all a very happy christmas and a very happy new year.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i should like to thank everyone for all the contributions, which reflect how complex an issue we are dealing with. allow me to react to some of the very clear and i am sure that we will honour this agreement. concerning the issue of politicisation of anti-dumping and countervailing measures, i think, actually, that we will see the opposite, because you know what the system is today: that a simple majority of the member states’ representatives can block a commission proposal. this would be much more difficult in the future because you would need a qualified majority of the member states representatives to block it. so i think that what we are doing here will actually strengthen the union approach and strengthen the position of the commission in the trade talks, exactly as prescribed and projected by the lisbon treaty. if you will allow me, i will conclude by underlining the importance of legal certainty in this matter because, of course, when we are dealing with sensitive issues like trade, like anti-dumping measures, like countervailing measures, we need to have very well established procedures and we need to have a clear division of roles and responsibilities. parliament needs the very clear scrutiny rights which have been given to it by the lisbon treaty, and we need the legal certainty to operate in this very important legislative area because you know how often these measures are disputed in various international fora. therefore, i would plead with the honourable members to support these proposals without amendment because i think they are really good for the position of the european union in world affairs.

mr president, in january 2012 400 spanish egg producers could disappear, around 30% of the total in my country, with a loss of production of 300 000 tonnes of eggs. the european union could stop producing those 80 million eggs, those 2 million tonnes, and we could only get them covered by imports from third countries, whose animal welfare standards are far below those of the european union, if we do not act very intelligently. this 1999 directive, which requires that the cages of laying hens be increased in size, requires us to act with intelligence and a possible view, because otherwise we will only be able to weaken european production and give extra opportunities, commercial opportunities, to third countries, where the space per bird is infinitely less than we currently have in the european union. it is a directive which requires a great deal of effort from european producers - in spain alone we can understand that the cost is some 600 million euros - but we must not forget, moreover, that it has an economic impact which extends to the egg industry and the food industry in general. i therefore ask for your support for the amendment by the ppe group to paragraph 2, which calls for a solution at least for responsible farms, for responsible industrialists, who are in the process of transforming their farms and who will have completed it by january 2012. we must support them in the conversion of these facilities and give them time to complete this process, thus avoiding irreparable damage to farms and preventing a situation of shortage on the community market from one day to the next, with consequent increases in consumer prices. it is a matter of respecting the directive, of giving the egg and egg product industry a chance, and also of respecting the right to animal welfare and the right of consumers to a reasonable price.
mr president, commissioner, as you will see, we in this house ensure that the rules are observed, even those which have not yet entered into force. if we extended this exercise to other sectors with deadlines, we would have to hold plenary sessions for 15 days. today we are talking about a sector which does not receive any aid from the cap and which is suffering from the increase in the price of feed. it is not easy for it to tackle additional costs, but it must do so to meet the high production standards we set for ourselves in the union. all indications are that by 1 january 2012 producers in many member states will not have been able to meet 100% of the deadline. it is estimated that 30% of production will be missing to meet the needs of the community market. the result: fresh eggs will be produced here - yes, they will be more expensive for the consumer - and those destined for processing will be bought abroad, thus closing off the part of european union production that went to that market. i hope that by then we will have more success in demanding reciprocity in our relations with third countries. the end: the standard will be mandatory from 2012. in the meantime, the commission can already enforce other existing rules, such as the electronic identification of sheep and goats, whose added value in terms of traceability and good veterinary conditions also has a direct impact on animal welfare.

in writing. − although it has chosen not to join the european economic area, switzerland has shown sustained interest in closer cooperation with the eu in the education, training and youth fields. initially, the legal bases for the eu education, training and youth programmes did not provide for participation by switzerland, but this changed in 2006 when parliament and council adopted decisions establishing the 2007-2013 ‘youth in action’ and lifelong learning programmes. in february 2008, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations on swiss participation in the two programmes. an agreement was reached in august 2009 and the council has already adopted a decision approving its signature and provisional application from 2011. under article 218(6) of the tfeu, the council has to obtain the consent of the european parliament before the agreement can enter into force. the parliament and council decisions establishing the ‘youth in action’ and lifelong learning programmes, adopted in 2006, already provided in principle for swiss participation. the agreement negotiated with the swiss authorities by the commission is quite adequate: it extends the benefits of the programmes to switzerland, while safeguarding the financial and other interests of the eu. the rapporteur therefore recommends that the parliament approve the council draft decision.
